L2: a child manifest recorded the Runner default limits rather than the pool limits that actually bounded the fan-out, which FR-43 and FR-72 make the audit record. The cause was two separate omissions: the pool did not pass its limits on the child RunConfig, and Runner._limits_for rebuilt a run own limits from three fields, so the three that M18 added fell back to their defaults for every run that set limits at all. Both are fixed, with a mutant each; provider limits are stripped from the child config because a RunConfig may not carry them under FR-43, and a test covers a pool built from a Runner own limits. The reviewer recorded three caveats, none blocking and all accepted as they stand: the adapter check for a provider that refuses response_format is a substring match, so an unrelated 400 naming the parameter costs one wasted retry while the final error stays correct; depth and parent are caller trusted with no ancestry check, so a caller that re-asserts depth can chain past the limit, which matches D13 and DECISION-35f4c3f4; and principal_context is passed by the caller rather than inherited automatically. Gates green on 96a80385 with 31 unit and 1499 regression, and the mutation run is 32 of 33 with D11 still declared, the depth field that nothing reads until M19.

decisions.title: M18 round 2 rejected: a child laundered taint it read through its own tools
decisions.text: The M18 round 2 reviewer, Fable 5.1, rejected the milestone at 2026-09-29T10:13:37Z on one blocking finding, M1, which the owner reproduced on both stores. The result provenance covered the briefing input_refs alone, so a child that fetched a page through a tool handed the text to its parent labelled origin model, trust trusted_source and untainted, while its own stored history showed the tool result marked untrusted with external_content and prompt_injection_risk. That is the laundering FR-70 forbids, and worse than round 1 L1 because the text crosses rather than an empty result. It is reachable with the shipped tools, two of which declare external provenance. Fixed: a child inputs are its briefing and whatever it read while running, so the pool reads the child own session history after the run, through a new underscored Runner._history_for, and folds the provenance of every tool result in it into the answer label. A pool that cannot read that history now fails the node rather than handing text to a parent with a label it cannot justify, which is declared for the next reviewer to judge, since it turns a store failure into a failed node. Also fixed, M2 from the same review: an input bytes were read before its provenance, so an input whose metadata failed reported clean although its content had been taken in; the provenance is read first, and a test pins both endings, nothing read staying clean and a known provenance surviving a failed read. Four mutants cover the two fixes. Carried as declared caveats, not fixed: M3, the manifest cannot distinguish a structured child from a plain one; M4, a pool limits replace the Runner per-tool limits for children, so a child can run more tools at once than the Runner would allow, which is recorded consistently but widens silently; M5, limits are counted per parent scope, so a nested tree can reach N plus N squared children at once; M6, an invalid JSON Schema is reported as the model failure; M8, SubagentResult.artifacts stays empty until tools get a run scope. The reviewer also noted that the M11 assertion changed in round 1 compares the stored limits against to_json itself, so a key dropped from to_json would vanish from both sides; that is recorded for the next pass. Gates green on c4fe9507 with 36 unit and 1504 regression, mutation 36 of 37 with D11 still declared.

decisions.title: M18 round 3 rejected: the round 2 fix read the store on the event loop, the third recurrence of that lesson
decisions.text: The M18 round 3 reviewer, Sonnet 5, rejected the milestone at 2026-09-29T12:28:30Z on one blocking finding, and the owner confirmed it by thread identity rather than by clock. SubagentPool._what_it_read, the round 2 fix for the taint laundering, called Runner._history_for directly: no await and no worker thread, so on Postgres it checked out a pooled connection and ran a SELECT on the event loop after every completed child, while the pool held a concurrency slot across it. DECISION-6b62d1f5 states the property flatly, that every store call made during a run goes through asyncio.to_thread, and KNOWLEDGE-c0f23fea records the same lesson from M7 round 1, that the offload was applied to the call sites someone looked at rather than asserted of every store call. This is its third recurrence. The owner judged it blocking above the reviewer own medium-high, because the enforcement test that exists for exactly this, test_no_store_call_runs_on_the_event_loop_thread_on_any_run_path, drives Runner.run across five paths and never touches SubagentPool, so the new call site was invisible to its guard. Fixed: the read is awaited through asyncio.to_thread, and the enforcement test gains a sixth path, a SubagentPool spawn, so the property is asserted of every way of making a store call rather than of five known ones. A mutant that restores the direct call is killed by that test, which is the evidence the guard now covers the site. Both earlier defects were confirmed closed by rerunning the earlier rounds own probes: the round 2 laundering case now reports untrusted with both taint flags, and the round 2 M2 case is clean for the right reason, because metadata fails before any content is read. The reviewer found no instance of the third defect the round 3 brief predicted; manifests for children and plain runs record what actually governed them. Two notes accepted: a FAIL line in its probe 3 is a probe bug comparing Message objects for membership, and its C2 note, that a tool wrapping a nested spawn cannot pass the grandchild real provenance, is an M19 gap because nothing in M18 wires a tool to spawn. The owner and the reviewer both agree with failing a node whose history cannot be read, with the rider that an un-offloaded read made that worse under fan-out; the read is now offloaded. Gates green on 21cc3067 with 36 unit and 1504 regression, mutation 37 of 38 with D11 still declared.

decisions.title: M18 round 4 caveats C1, C2 and C4 become M18a, specified before M19
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-07. The round 4 review approved M18 with five non-blocking caveats. C1 (RunConfig validates neither depth nor output_schema), C2 (Briefing.expected_output_schema unvalidated, raising after _admit consumed a task count) and C4 (the thread-identity guard enumerates paths, the third recurrence of KNOWLEDGE-c0f23fea) are specified as FR-79 to FR-82 in a new task M18a, sequenced BEFORE M19 so the loop-thread guard exists before the orchestrator adds store call sites of its own. Rejected: amending M19 (mixes a validation and test-infrastructure change into the highest-risk milestone, and one reviewer would review the orchestrator and the guard together) and appending after M20 (two more milestones add call sites first). C5, the live example leaving rows under example-tenant, stays outside NFR-16 scope.

decisions.title: C3 resolved: a briefed input gets a provenance-manifest entry and a data-only marker
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-07, answering M18 round 4 caveat C3: a briefed input reached the child user message with no data-only marker and no provenance-manifest entry, and only the result label carried the taint; the live structured child echoed the injected phrase and the example checked a substring. Both halves are specified: FR-83 adds a provenance-manifest entry for every briefed input (uri or hash, origin, instruction authority, trust zone, taint flags) as request metadata, which is the enforceable half under ADR-26; FR-84 adds a delimited data-only marker in the briefing text as signalling only, leaving ADR-17 intact (provenance informs policy, never instructs the model), and changes the example to assert the result provenance instead of a substring. Rejected: marker only (nothing downstream can act on it) and defer to P2-D25 (leaves the child own context the one place taint is unrepresented).

decisions.title: M18a clarifications of FR-79 and FR-82: depth 0 is the top-level run, and the refusal is a module switch the test harness turns on
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-07 at M18a pre-flight. (1) FR-79 says depth must be an int of 1 or more and AC-64 refuses 0, but RunConfig.depth defaults to 0 and P2-D21 makes the orchestrator depth 0. Read as: a run with no parent_run_id is depth 0; a run with a parent_run_id must have depth from 1 to 2**31-1; a bool or non-int is refused either way. AC-64 zero case is a child at depth 0. Rejected: depth None by default (changes the field type and stops recording the orchestrator as 0) and refusing 0 always (contradicts P2-D21). (2) FR-82 on under tests and off in production is decided by a module-level switch, postgres.REFUSE_ON_EVENT_LOOP, False in code and turned on for every test by the autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py; AC-66 off case flips it per test. Rejected: an environment variable (covers tests only where every runner sets it), a flag on Persistence (threads through every store constructor and still needs conftest to flip it) and detecting pytest in sys.modules (a production process that imports pytest would start failing runs). The refusal raises RuntimeError naming the store method, inside a run it reaches Runner total boundary as any other failure (INVARIANT-af776957).

decisions.title: M18a FR-81 finding: 37 tests read the store on the loop; the reads are offloaded, the fixture is not narrowed
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-07. With the FR-81 autouse fixture and the FR-82 refusal on and nothing else changed, the full suite gave 38 failed and 37 teardown errors. 37 were test code reading the store synchronously from async tests after a run, at 8 helper lines in 6 approved files: history() in test_concurrency.py:181 (18) and test_run_handles.py:175 (5), start_run in test_artifacts.py:125 (6) and test_phase2_readiness.py:199 (3), PostgresTrace.reconstruct in test_golden_eval.py:705 (2) and :400 (1) and test_persistence.py:803 (1), get_run in test_persistence.py:1153 (1). No call came from agentsdk: no run path violates FR-20. The 38th was a defect in the new fixture, which wrapped each _pool() call in a fresh object and broke the one-pool-per-DSN identity test; fixed by caching one wrapper per pool, which changes nothing the fixture catches. Resolution: the reads are offloaded with asyncio.to_thread at their call sites and listed in the round 1 review prompt. Rejected: narrowing the fixture to calls made inside a run (a hook, tool or pool path outside the run task would slip through, the KNOWLEDGE-c0f23fea shape) and an opt-out marker (KNOWLEDGE-0e7be079).

decisions.title: M18a: DECISION-53ee27f6 revised: RunConfig.depth is None unless the pool placed the run
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-07, revising part (1) of DECISION-53ee27f6 on new evidence. The first reading (a run with a parent_run_id must be depth 1 or more) refused FR-21 public usage: RunConfig(parent_run_id=...) without depth is what scripts/07 and seven approved tests build, and all eight raised in the full suite. Now depth is int or None, default None; None is a run the pool did not place (every top-level run, the orchestrator depth 0 of P2-D21, an FR-21 child built by application code); a depth that is set must be an int from 1 to 2**31-1 and never a bool, with or without a parent, so AC-64 zero class is refused literally. Nothing reads depth (D11), so the type change costs nothing today. Rejected: keeping the first reading and adding depth to callers (changes the FR-21 contract no FR asks to change) and accepting 0 everywhere (AC-64 would need amending). Part (2), the FR-82 module switch, stands.

decisions.title: Publishing amended: the session-folder name is filtered, and the ADR-12 reports may differ
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-07, amending DECISION-a3c77601. Publishing had been blocked since M15, so GitHub held M14 as its last commit: a dry run of .git/publish-filter/publish.sh failed verify.py with 9 problems. Review prompts from M16 on name the agent session scratchpad, whose folder name writes the local user folder and cloud-folder path in a dashed form that no rule matched; and M15 evals/adr12/reports/adr12-comparison-2026-09-16.json records local paths, which the filter scrubbed but verify.py refused, because it allowed filtered changes only under .genesis/ and in SPEC.md. Fixed in .git/publish-filter, which is never published: rules.txt gains a regex rule for the dashed folder name, ordered before the bare username rule; verify.py MAY_DIFFER also allows evals/adr12/reports/, which holds measured data rather than code, so every code file must still be byte-identical. The rebuilt copy verified with 0 problems over 722 file versions and every message, authors, dates and commit count unchanged, and phase-2 was pushed as a fast-forward from 064a670 to 26900a1 (M18a); main unchanged at 51e48e7. git-filter-repo is pinned at 2.47.0 in a throwaway venv so filtering stays deterministic. Rejected: dropping the report from the published copy (GitHub would lose the M15 measurements) and not publishing.

decisions.title: M19 clarifications of FR-73 to FR-76: a run with a plan tool, outputs as briefed inputs, what replans, one governor re-split
decisions.text: Owner decisions 2026-10-07 at M19 pre-flight. (1) The orchestrator is one Runner run at depth 0 whose agent has one plan tool: the model submits a plan as the tool arguments, validated against the shipped plan schema; the tool, which receives its RunScope (FR-76), stores the PlanVersion, executes the DAG through SubagentPool with children linked to this run, and returns each node outcome as its result. A failed plan returns to the model, whose next call of the tool is the replan, so replanning happens inside the same run, counted against the orchestrator reserve and bounded by max_replans. Rejected: a Python driver writing run records itself (a second way of recording a run) and a caller-supplied plan (moves FR-73 counted planning and FR-75 automatic replanning out of M19). (2) A done node output is stored as an artifact in the run scope carrying its SubagentResult provenance, and each dependent receives its dependencies outputs as briefed inputs beside its own input_refs, so taint follows the edges through FR-70 and FR-83. Rejected: dependencies as ordering only, since input_refs are fixed at plan time and a planner cannot name an artifact that does not exist yet. (3) Every node failure is replannable except budget_exceeded and cancellation, including acceptance_criterion_failed, output_contract_violation, criterion_not_available, a failed child run and a refused spawn; max_replans and the run ceiling bound it. Rejected: replanning only when the plan was wrong. (4) One BudgetGovernor per orchestrator run: a replan keeps all spend and every done node reservation and splits what remains unallocated among the new version not-done nodes by the M17 rules, through one new governor method. Rejected: a fresh governor per version, which would carve the orchestrator and unallocated reserves out again on every replan.

decisions.title: M19 round 1 rejected: a failed plan ended the run completed, and taint reached the orchestrator under a clean label
decisions.text: Round 1, Sonnet 5 standing in for Fable 5.1, rejected M19 at 17:50:11Z on source hash 3fdc0710; the owner reproduced D1. D1 (blocking): a failed plan could end the run completed, because only CancelledError out of a version set the run unresolved: a child answer over the artifact store cap raised out of the plan tool, the model answered, and the run completed with its only node cancelled. D2: a failed tool_succeeds criterion put the tool text into the node reason and dropped its provenance. D3: the provenance of a node was refreshed on every child while its answer was kept from the last done version, so a rerun that failed reported the old tainted answer under the new clean label. D4 (low): a retired budget record was keyed node@vN, which a planner chosen node id could collide with, losing spend from the allocation record. Repairs: D1 is made total rather than patched on one path. RunConfig.pending_failure, set by Orchestrator.config, makes an orchestrator run unresolved from its start, so a run that never completes a plan version cannot end completed, including one whose model never calls run_plan or whose every document is refused by schema validation; run_plan sets the run unresolved on entry and on any exception, and only a done version clears it; a node is total, so a failure inside one node, an unstorable output included (output_not_stored), fails that node and leaves its siblings. D2 and D3 are repaired at their common cause: the report and its taken_in are built from one record, every label of what a node report says (its child provenance whatever its status, a criterion tool result provenance when its text is shown), and an answer only for a node done in this version, stored with its own label. D4: adopt checks before it moves anything, gives a retired record the first free key, never retires a kept record twice, and refuses a new node whose id is a kept record. Each finding has a test written first that failed on the round 1 code. Reviewer caveats kept in view, not repaired: AttributedArtifacts scopes writes but not reads or deletes, since the store is bound to tenant and project rather than run; ToolScope underscored fields are accepted as in-process trusted code (D13) with a narrower type recommended. Round 2 goes to Fable 5.1, as Sonnet 5 has reviewed M18 rounds 1 and 3, M18a round 1 and M19 round 1.

decisions.title: M19 round 2 rejected: a done side-effecting node was rerun after a version omitted it; artifact_exists accepted any run artifact
decisions.text: Round 2, Opus 5 standing in for Fable 5.1, rejected M19 at 12:12:13Z on source hash 285bdb1f; the owner reproduced D5. D5 (blocking): the run remembered what was done one version deep, because run.statuses was replaced by each version and _carried compared only with the version before, so a version omitting a done side-effecting node followed by one naming it again ran it a second time; side_effecting defaults to True, so this is the invoice sent twice, and the plan shape is the model choice. Repair: a run-lifetime record of every done node (the version it was done in, its definition then, whether it had side effects), written in a finally so a node done before a raise or a cancellation is remembered, and consulted by _carried: a node that had side effects is carried whenever it reappears, a pure one when unchanged since it was done. Second, from the review caveats: artifact_exists verified any artifact of the tenant and project, so an artifact another run left there satisfied it; now the artifact must have this orchestrator run or one of its child runs as source_run before its hash is checked, and the report names each done node output uri so a replan can require it, since a planner cannot know a uri before it is written. Tests for both written first and failing on the round 2 code. Caveats recorded, not repaired: a tool declaring a RunScope parameter receives the Runner through ToolScope._runner and can reach any tenant artifact store, in any run, orchestrated or not; this is in-process trusted code under D13 and could build a store directly, but it is wider than NFR-2 multi-tenant by construction suggests, and a narrower tool scope type should replace the underscored fields; a hand-built RunConfig without pending_failure can reach run_plan and end completed with no plan, reachable only by bypassing Orchestrator.config. The round 2 reviewer first ran the gates without --timeout and recorded regression:fail, then reran them correctly: 44 and 1583 passed on 285bdb1f. Round 3 rotation is tight: Opus 5.5 implemented; Sonnet 5, Fable 5.1 and Opus 5 have reviewed; Fable 5.1 is least recently exposed.

decisions.title: M19 round 3, D6: a node finished in a batch whose settling raised is recorded as it ended
decisions.text: Round 3 (Sonnet 5 standing in for Fable 5.1) rejected M19 on D6: asyncio.wait(FIRST_COMPLETED) can return several finished node tasks; _execute settled them one at a time, and when settling the first raised (a transient store error on a transition), the rest stayed in running, their tasks already complete and their tools already run; the except branch then marked them cancelled, so run.done never recorded them, the replan ran them again, and the persisted state said cancelled for work that happened. Repair: after cancelling and awaiting the unfinished tasks, the except branch settles every task that returned a result with its own status, reason and labels before marking anything else cancelled; settle() sets the in-memory status before it writes, so a store that fails again still leaves run.done true (the persisted row then stays at running, never a false cancelled). Test written first and failing on the round 3 code (3 tool calls, not 2): test_d6_a_sibling_finished_in_the_same_batch_as_a_faulting_transition_is_done_not_cancelled. Two mutants added (no harvest; harvested recorded cancelled). Round 4 rotation: Opus 5 (the owner's default; Fable 5.1 failed on first call three rounds running). Round 4 re-covers what round 3 left partial: FR-76 attribution first-hand including an Optional[RunScope] annotation, the Postgres half of F2/F4 run on its own, and a USD-ceiling budget case.

decisions.title: M19 round 4, D6 again: a fault no longer cancels the nodes already running
decisions.text: Round 4 (Opus 5) rejected M19: the round 3 repair of D6 cancelled the unfinished node tasks and then harvested only tasks that had returned, so a sibling still in flight after its child had run its tool -- awaiting its output write -- was cancelled, recorded cancelled and rerun on the replan; the reviewer's unchanged round 3 probe still reproduced it 5 of 6 times. The round 3 test parked both tasks behind a barrier after Orchestrator._node returned, so nothing was ever in flight and it could only see the path the repair covered. Repair: a non-cancellation exception out of the scheduler (a transition the store refused) no longer cancels anything; the version awaits every running node to its end, then settles each with its own result, and only then marks what never started cancelled. A real cancellation still cancels and awaits every child at once, and a cancellation that arrives while the nodes finish after a fault cancels them and is re-raised. Harvesting before cancelling would not have been enough: in the reviewer's probe the sibling had not returned when the fault landed. Tests, the first two written first and failing on the round 4 code (3 tool calls, not 2): a deterministic in-flight case (b held at its output write after its tool ran; a's done transition faults only once b is there); the reviewer's unheld shape repeated 8 times per run; and a guard that a cancellation during the wait still ends the run cancelled with b cancelled. Three mutants added. Non-blocking round 4 findings carried, not repaired here: _with_scope matches the annotation by literal name, so RunScope | None, an alias or a subclass receives no scope (FR-76 says a tool that declares one receives it); a criterion whose own check raises is reported node_error rather than naming the criterion (FR-74); _check's emit closure ignores its event_type. Round 5 rotation: Fable 5.1 retried first, falling back to Sonnet 5.

decisions.title: M20 clarifications of FR-77 and FR-78: a policy on RunConfig, reported plus estimated tokens, a known window, append-only compaction
decisions.text: Owner, M20 pre-flight 2026-10-09. (1) Which runs: RunConfig gains context_policy, None by default. Orchestrator.config() and the subagent pool set one, so orchestrated runs see only their profile's tools and compact; a plain run sends exactly what it sends today (NFR-12, NFR-15) and DECISION-ca1ad3e0 keeps governing it; an application may opt in. (2) Measuring the threshold: the provider's prompt_tokens from the run's last call plus a characters/4 estimate of the messages added since, so a large tool result is caught before it is sent; no tokenizer (NFR-21). (3) An unknown context window: ContextPolicy takes an explicit context_window, else the ModelRegistry's max_context_tokens; a compacting policy on a model with neither is a configuration error where the run is configured, naming the model, following P2-D20's USD precedent. (4) What compaction replaces: the instructions, the original task and the most recent turns stay whole, a tool call never separated from its results; the middle is replaced by one summary. Stored messages are never rewritten: the summary is appended as a marked message and assembly starts from the latest one, so the messages table stays the full record NFR-3 relies on. The replaced messages also go into the artifact FR-78 names, and the summary's taint rides in the provenance manifest as a briefed input's does (FR-83).

decisions.title: M20 caveats C1 and C3 become M20a, specified before Phase 3
decisions.text: Owner, 2026-10-09, after M20 round 1 approval (KNOWLEDGE-cc4d686c). C1: ContextCompacted records tokens_before and tokens_after on one basis, the whole-request estimate built from the view before and after the compaction, and keeps the number that decided it as threshold_measure with threshold_basis naming its basis (the provider's prompt_tokens for the last request plus an estimate of what was added since, or the whole-request estimate); chosen over labelling the two existing bases, which would leave a reader comparing different things, and over waiting for the next call's report, which would delay the event. C3: the summary message and its ContextCompacted event are written in one transaction on Postgres, as M19 F4 writes a transition and its event, with the same rule in memory; the artifact is written first, so an artifact with no compaction is the only possible leftover; chosen over emitting the event first, which moves the gap rather than closing it, and over recording the gap in the terminal event. Specified as FR-85, FR-86, AC-68 and AC-69 in a task M20a before Phase 3. C4 to C6 stay carried.

decisions.title: Phase 3 P3-D1 to P3-D4: two increments, a ledger per run, a contention exit signal, carried items first
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-10, at the start of Phase 3, from an inventory of everything the design documents and records say about it (no Phase 3 exit signal, ledger mechanics, cache defaults or critic contract was written anywhere). P3-D1: Phase 3 is specified in two increments, following the rule that split Phase 2 (DECISION-ce3b0e78): increment 1 is the evidence substrate in full requirements -- immutable EvidenceSourceVersion, the tenant- and auth-scoped resource cache (ADR-31), the ledger of claims with supersede history (ADR-07), claim-lock with backoff (ADR-08); increment 2, the confidence gate, the conditional critic and ADR-15 calibration, is outlined with its open decisions and specified once the ledger exists, because the critic verifies claims. P3-D2: a ledger belongs to one top-level run and is shared by its children; source versions are durable and found again through the scoped cache, but claims are not reused across runs until governed learning (I-23, after Phases 3 and 4) decides how. This follows ADR-16's session-scoped ledger and resolves the local notes calling the ledger reusable across runs. P3-D3: the exit signal is contention on a synthetic task, as v0.2 states the goal (dedup and confidence gate hold up under contention) and as Stage 1 requires (no real Research Analyst): overlapping subagents fetch overlapping sources and record overlapping claims in one run; each source version is fetched once per cache scope, each claim is stored once with every contributor and its sources, supersede history is readable, no cache hit crosses a tenant, and taint is carried from source to claim; increment 2 adds that the gate calls the critic only when its signals require it, at most once, and that the critic never clears taint on its own. P3-D4: a small first milestone, M21, opens Phase 3 with M20a's carried F1 and F2 (KNOWLEDGE-afac039f) and decides M20's C4 to C6 (KNOWLEDGE-cc4d686c) or records them as declared limits, so the ledger starts on a clean base.

decisions.title: Phase 3 increment 1: sources, cache, claims, lock, taint and milestones (P3-D5 to P3-D12)
decisions.text: Owner accepted on 2026-10-10, before any increment 1 requirement was written. P3-D5: a source version is captured automatically by the built-in fetch, and any tool may declare itself a source the same way: every fetch records an immutable EvidenceSourceVersion (canonical URI, retrieval time, content hash, cache scope, prior version), its content stored as an M13 artifact, and the tool result's provenance names the version, so a claim cites exactly what was read; an explicit record_source tool was rejected because a model that forgets to call it leaves a claim citing nothing. P3-D6: the resource cache serves: cache-aside at the tool layer (ADR-16), a fetch whose key has a fresh version in a scope the caller may read is served with no network and recorded as a hit, concurrent fetches of one key wait for one fetch (singleflight), freshness is a policy TTL defaulting to one hour, and a stale version is refetched as the new version's prior. P3-D7: the built-in fetch caches at PROJECT scope by default; TENANT and PUBLIC_GLOBAL only by explicit configuration per tool or allowlisted host; SESSION and NO_CACHE available. A mistake costs a refetch, never a cross-tenant leak (ADR-31). P3-D8: claims enter through tools: record_claim(statement, supporting and contradicting source versions, confidence) and supersede_claim(old, new, why), for any agent whose profile includes them, each visible in the event stream; parsing claims from node output was rejected because only orchestrated nodes could contribute. P3-D9: claims deduplicate on a hash of the statement after Unicode NFC, case-folding and whitespace collapse; every contributor and source of a duplicate attaches to the one stored claim; paraphrases stay distinct, and merging them is left to increment 2's critic. P3-D10: claim-lock is singleflight per key -- a resource key for a fetch, a claim key for a record -- with one holder and waiters taking its result; when the holder fails one waiter retries with exponential backoff (base 0.2 s, factor 2, jitter, at most 3 attempts) and the call then fails naming the key; a Postgres advisory lock across processes and an asyncio lock within one; a lease with expiry is left to Phase 6's durability work. P3-D11: a claim's provenance is ContentProvenance.from_model over every supporting and contradicting source version and the contributor's own inputs, so a claim drawn from untrusted pages is untrusted; nothing in increment 1 lowers it, and whether a verification may is increment 2's open decision (ADR-26). P3-D12: increment 1 is M21 the carried items (P3-D4); M22 EvidenceSourceVersion and the scoped resource cache with fetch recording versions (migration 0010, example 19); M23 the ledger -- claims, sources, contributors, supersede history, record_claim and supersede_claim (0011, example 20); M24 claim-lock and backoff under contention and the exit-signal run on both stores (example 21).

decisions.title: Phase 3 increment 1: the spec-level choices of the reviewed draft accepted
decisions.text: Owner accepted on 2026-10-10, after the read-only spec review (KNOWLEDGE-6585cf8f), seven choices the second draft of FR-87 to FR-96 makes beyond P3-D1 to P3-D12: (1) every cache hit on a version outside the reader's tenant and project, a TENANT version from another project included, is served as a copy carrying none of the origin's identifiers, so every citable version is in the claim's own tenant and project; (2) FR-91 supersedes FR-38's final-URL source: a fetch names its version's uri, the final URL is the version's final_uri, the four tests asserting the old value are edited, and a fetch with no run scope keeps the old behaviour; (3) claims deduplicate against active claims only, a statement matching only a superseded claim records a new active claim, and a supersession onto another active statement is refused; (4) only 2xx responses are cached; (5) claim-lock uses session-level Postgres advisory locks in a lock space of their own, waited on by polling pg_try_advisory_lock behind a per-key asyncio lock, with full jitter, and when the retrying waiter's attempts run out every waiter fails naming the key; (6) the new events SourceFetched, SourceServed, ClaimRecorded and ClaimSuperseded with the fields FR-91, FR-93 and FR-94 state; (7) the in-memory session store keys a run's history by tenant, project and run id.

decisions.title: M21: F1 and F2 repaired first; C4 and C5 declared, C6 repaired at plan submission (FR-88)
decisions.text: Owner, 2026-10-10. F1 and F2 were repaired before the rest of M21, as FR-87: a sink naming no scope gets the two writes it got before M20a on both stores; a sink naming a scope must name the run's tenant, project and run id; the Runner binds its in-memory session store per run, keying history by tenant, project and run id, through a context variable so every write still goes through InMemorySessionStore's own public methods (a first version that wrote past append broke three approved tests that patch it, and was replaced); unbound reads by run id keep working. Baseline before M21: 1647 passed on f19dc611, the code unchanged since M20a's gate. FR-88: C4 declared -- the manifest records configuration, written in one piece at run start (FR-11), so tools_sent means the tools the run's agent is sent, stated in the README limits and the manifest docstring and asserted by a test; repair (writing it with the first request) was rejected because the manifest would stop being written at start. C5 declared -- an AgentSpec may carry its own permission_policy; under a ContextPolicy the agent is still sent only its tool_profile's tools, so a tool the policy permits but the profile does not name is invisible and refused ToolNotFound; stated and tested; a checker able to list what it permits comes with Phase 4's policy engine, and a per-tool query was rejected because an argument-dependent checker cannot answer it. C6 repaired -- when run_plan receives a plan, every role a node to be run names is checked against the Runner (its model resolves, its context window is known under the policy, its other configuration passes) before anything is adopted, stored or spawned; a role that cannot run ends the plan failed and unreplannable with the configuration error naming the role and model, and nothing is spent; reporting it as spawn_refused mid-run, or declaring it, were rejected.

decisions.title: M21 round 1 rejected: unbound in-memory calls raised under concurrency; a lock and a run index
decisions.text: Round 1 (Sonnet 5) rejected M21: InMemorySessionStore._unbound iterated the store's dict with a bare comprehension while other threads added runs, so an unbound append or read raised 'dictionary changed size during iteration' -- 8 of 8 attempts in the reviewer's probe, 0 of 8 on HEAD c244f23 under the same load; a regression M21 introduced, mostly on the write path, contradicting FR-87's promise that an unbound caller keeps its behaviour; each unbound call was also an O(runs) scan. Everything else held, each negative with a mutant behind it: F1 and F2 across 14 sink shapes on both stores, C6 with no side effect and no false refusal, and C4 and C5 as declared. Repair: one lock over the store's dict and a new run id to keys index, so an unbound call finds its run without a scan; the take-back, append and history copy under the same lock, and no lock is held across a sink's emit. A list() copy alone was rejected because it keeps the scan. Test written first and failing on the round 1 code (1599 errors on its first attempt): six threads bind new runs while six make unbound appends and reads, eight attempts, nothing patched, with the thread switch interval at a microsecond -- the first mutation run showed that at the default 5 ms a restored scan could finish between switches and survive. Two mutants added; 13 of 13 killed. Round 2 rotation: Fable 5.1, falling back to Opus 5.

decisions.title: M21a: the four M21 caveats repaired or declared before M22 (owner)
decisions.text: Owner decisions 2026-10-10, before M22's pre-flight, on the four caveats carried by KNOWLEDGE-8e29cfe3. (1) Repaired: InMemorySessionStore.append_with_event derives the run's key once and the write and the take-back both act on that key, so an unbound combined write racing a run's first bound write cannot file the run id under two keys; rejected: declaring it. (2) Repaired: the first tenant and project to bind a run id adopt the history written to that id unbound before it, as HEAD before M21 merged them; a second tenant binding the same id still gets a history of its own and unbound reads across two tenants are still refused; rejected: declaring the loud refusal. (3) Declared, with proof of unreachability: inside a bound combined write a sink that writes a different run is refused, as FR-87 requires; the Runner always passes the run's own sink, so a test asserts every sink the Runner builds (top-level runs, subagents, orchestrator children) names its own run; rejected: two writes for a foreign sink, which would weaken the F2 repair. (4) Kept declared (M20a): on Postgres a scope-less custom sink whose emit fails leaves the summary without its event; rejected: emitting inside the transaction (holds the run's messages lock across custom code, which hangs if that sink writes the same run) and a compensating delete (breaks FR-9's insert-only store); a test asserts the declared behaviour. Governance: the owner chose a separate task, M21a, ahead of M22. Genesis cannot reopen the plan while a task is active and has no command to clear the active task, so the owner approved one manual edit of .genesis/project.json: M22's active pointer cleared and M22 returned to queued, and after task add, M21a moved ahead of M22 in the task list so plan approval activates it first. Nothing else in the state file is edited by hand.

decisions.title: M22 pre-flight: M21a review caveats settled; ledger_run_id pulled forward; example 19 offline and live
decisions.text: Owner decisions 2026-10-10 at M22's pre-flight. (1) The three caveats carried by KNOWLEDGE-bbd190e1 are settled before M22's own work, inside M22 and disclosed in its review: C1, the README row for caveat 4 corrected to any sink that names no scope or cannot write inside the store's transaction; C2 repaired, an unbound in-memory combined write whose sink names the run is filed under the sink's tenant and project, with a test that fails without it, added to tests/test_carried_caveats.py; C4, AC-75 reworded to the per-run bound view the Runner hands its loop, and FR-97 extended with C1 and C2. The owner permitted signing the spec and plan approvals again as siva-rgb (owner); M22 is requeued through the CLI first so plan approval makes it active again, with no manual state edit. (2) FR-92's ledger_run_id is pulled forward into M22 so SESSION scope reaches the top-level run as FR-90 says: a top-level run's own id, set by the pool on every subagent and orchestrator child; rejected: SESSION as this run only until M23. (3) Example 19 runs offline against a local server with a fake model and live against one allowlisted public page with the real model, read back from Postgres and removed by its run ids; rejected: offline only.

decisions.title: M23 pre-flight: M22 caveats 1 to 5 repaired, 6 declared; the ledger store serialises per key
decisions.text: Owner decisions 2026-10-11 at M23's pre-flight on the six caveats of KNOWLEDGE-2763f57b. Repaired inside M23: (1) the orchestrator's criterion executor scope carries the run's ledger_run_id and resource cache as the node scope does; (2) a test runs an orchestrator as a child and asserts its children share the top-level ledger, so the inheritance no longer rests on an orchestrator never being a child; (3) canonical_uri normalises the host as the fetch tool's allowlist does (lowercase, trailing dot removed, IDNA), the path still as sent, so http://h and http://h/ remain distinct keys, declared; (4) a fetch whose version cannot be recorded removes the artifact it stored; (5) ToolScope refuses a non-canonical ledger_run_id as RunConfig does. Declared: (6) own-first means a tool widened to a broader scope keeps serving its own narrower version until it expires. Rejected: repairing 1 and 2 only; repairing all six. Concurrency: the ledger store checks for an active claim and writes under a lock on (ledger, statement key), a transaction advisory lock on PostgreSQL and a lock in memory, so concurrent records of one new statement store one claim; M24 adds singleflight for the work. Rejected: duplicates until M24. The owner permitted re-signing the spec and plan approvals as siva-rgb (owner); FR-89, FR-90, FR-92 and FR-93 are edited; M23 is requeued through the CLI so plan approval reactivates it.

decisions.title: M23: claims cite a fetched URL as well as a version uri
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-11 during M23. Writing example 20 showed a live model cannot cite a source version: the fetch result's text does not show its urn:agentsdk:source uri, and the request's provenance manifest is not sent to the provider. record_claim and supersede_claim therefore also accept a URL the run has fetched, and cite the version that run was most recently given for it: the newest tool result in the run's history whose version has that canonical URI, or whose final URI canonicalises to it. A URL the run never fetched, even one another run fetched, is refused naming it; version uris still work. The fetch tool's output is unchanged. Rejected: the fetch result naming its version on a first line, which would change M22's approved output and tests; doing both. FR-93 is edited and the owner permitted re-signing the spec and plan as siva-rgb (owner); M23 is requeued through the CLI so plan approval reactivates it.

decisions.title: M24 pre-flight: M23 caveats 1 to 5 repaired; example 21 offline and live
decisions.text: Owner decisions 2026-10-11 at M24's pre-flight on the five caveats of KNOWLEDGE-5d3124ff, all repaired inside M24. (1) Both ledger stores check that every cited version is in the claim's tenant and project, and raise the contribution's labels to cover every version it cites, so a direct store caller cannot record a cross-tenant citation or a contribution cleaner than its sources, and migration 0011's comment becomes true (the migration file is not edited; its checksum is recorded). (2) supersede takes its two advisory locks in the order of their hashtext values, deduplicated, so colliding keys can never cross and deadlock. (3) Cite-by-URL ranks the run's own tool results above its briefed inputs. (4) The key normalises NFC, then casefold, then NFC again. (5) record_claim and supersede_claim read back only their own claim. Rejected: declaring 4; repairing 1 only. Example 21 runs offline (also a gate test on both stores) and live through an orchestrated plan against example.com and iana.org; rejected: offline only. FR-92 and FR-93 are edited; the owner permitted re-signing the spec and plan as siva-rgb (owner); M24 is requeued through the CLI so plan approval reactivates it.

decisions.title: M24a: the claim-lock's caveats C1 to C4 settled before increment 2 (owner)
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-11 on M24's approval (KNOWLEDGE-4301be95): complete M24, then a follow-up task M24a before Phase 3 increment 2 is specified, settling C1 (the database lock always unlocked and the pooled connection always returned under repeated cancellation, replacing a cleanup that suppressed a re-delivered CancelledError), C3 and C4 (at most three attempts per failure episode in all, counting a cancelled attempt and a waiter's own failure) and C2 (lock keys encoded so no two reaches collide). Specified as FR-98 and AC-76, with its own gates and independent review. C5 to C7 and example 21's vacuous taint check on the uncited correction are carried to increment 2's pre-flight. Rejected: carrying everything to increment 2. The owner permitted signing the spec and plan as siva-rgb (owner); no task is active, so the plan is reopened through the CLI with no manual state edit.

decisions.title: Phase 3 increment 2: what the gate judges, outcomes, trust and paraphrases (P3-D13 to P3-D16)
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-11, at the start of Phase 3 increment 2, from an inventory finding that the design fixes only rule signals first, a critic called only when required and at most once, the critic never clearing taint, and ADR-15 calibration from externally validated outcomes with a manual fallback. P3-D13: the gate judges an orchestrated node after its deterministic criteria pass -- its answer and the claims it recorded -- and calls the critic at most once per node; every verdict is recorded as an EvidenceVerification on the node and its claims; claims recorded outside a plan get signals but no critic. P3-D14: approved leaves the node done; corrected leaves it done with the critic answer, carrying the taint of both, and any claim it corrects is superseded through supersede_claim so history keeps both; escalate fails the node with critic_escalated, which replanning handles. P3-D15: no verification raises a claim trust or clears its taint in this increment, neither the critic (P3-D3) nor an external outcome; raising to VALIDATED waits for the Phase 4 ApprovalManager as an explicit audited decision (ADR-26). P3-D16: paraphrases are never merged; the critic may name claims it judges paraphrases in its verification, advisory only, and dedup stays the exact normalised hash.

decisions.title: Phase 3 increment 2: trigger, signals, calibration, critic, carried items and milestones (P3-D17 to P3-D22)
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-11. P3-D17: the gate runs on a node carrying a critic criterion, or on every node when the run GatePolicy says so; rule signals decide, so clean signals satisfy the criterion with no model call and the critic is called only when a signal fires. P3-D18: named rule signals over the node claims -- a claim with no supporting source, a claim with a contradicting source, fewer than min_sources supporting versions (default 1), a lowest contributor confidence below the threshold (default 0.7, None counting as below), and a node that recorded no claim when its criterion requires claims -- each switchable in GatePolicy; the critic is called if any fires, and the event names the signals that fired. P3-D19: record_validation stores a test result, known-answer fixture, downstream outcome or human adjudication for a claim or node as an external EvidenceVerification; calibration is a computed report per signal and threshold against external outcomes with a suggested threshold, and never changes configuration itself (governed learning, I-23). P3-D20: the critic is a configured subagent: GatePolicy names a critic AgentSpec, no tools by default, run as a child through the SubagentPool so budget, depth, taint, events and manifests apply, briefed with the node answer, its claims and the cited source versions content as data-only inputs, answering a fixed verdict schema; with no critic configured a critic criterion is refused as today. P3-D21: milestones M25 carried items; M26 EvidenceVerification (migration 0012), GatePolicy, the rule signals, events and record_validation; M27 the critic, the critic criterion available, outcome mapping and correction by supersede (example 22); M28 the calibration report and the exit signal run under contention with the gate (example 23). P3-D22: examples offline on both stores as gate tests and live against the gateway with an output-token limit. Carried items (KNOWLEDGE-06a8cf2f, KNOWLEDGE-4301be95): M25 repairs B1 (a waiter cancelled in backoff spends an attempt), W2 (KeyboardInterrupt absorbed in _finished), K1 (KeyFailed with no cause), P1 (ledger store lock names pipe-joined), P2 (manifest spec_material pipe-joined), C5 (a waited non-2xx records no wait), C7 (requirements bookkeeping) and example 21 vacuous taint check, each with a test that fails without it; W1 (an unbounded wait on a hung thread) and C6 (the holder keeps a pooled connection) are declared limits; B2 (a success between failures does not restore the budget) is kept as FR-98 states and declared, asserted by the approved test_c4.

decisions.title: Phase 3 increment 2: the spec-level choices of the reviewed draft accepted
decisions.text: Owner accepted on 2026-10-11, after the read-only spec review, the choices the second draft of FR-99 to FR-108 makes beyond P3-D13 to P3-D22: (1) agent_spec_hash is written v2 colon hex from M25, superseding FR-31 unchanged-hash statement, with no migration at M25; (2) B1 amends FR-98 so a waiter cancelled in backoff spends no attempt; (3) SourceUncached is a new event for a waited non-2xx fetch, and a waited fetch that raises records no wait, declared; (4) the critic draws on the node reservation, held until the gate ends, a reservation that cannot call fails the node budget_exceeded unreplanned, the critic counts in concurrency and task limits with node id node_id#critic; (5) the gate judges claims with a contribution from this execution child run only, deterministic criteria all run first, thin_support excludes unsupported, low_confidence excludes critic contributions, a gate_all_nodes node with no claims is cleared; (6) the verdict schema is built per node with enums of its claims and briefed versions, a corrected answer must satisfy the node output schema, and a correction losing a race fails the node and replans; (7) answer and claims rendering stored as artifacts before the critic, the critic has no tools, the briefing is capped by max_briefing_chars (default 200000) and fails over it, critic verifications written last naming applied and refused corrections; (8) record_validation and calibration_report are Runner methods, verifications live in the ledger store, node subjects checked against plan state; (9) calibration counts per gate row at gate time against the latest outcome, thresholds k/20, suggested threshold None below min_outcomes, with no incorrect outcome, or when none flags all.

decisions.title: Increment 2 tasks: the regression gate added by one manual edit (owner)
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-11. M25 to M28 were added with the regression gate flag and its value passed as one shell argument, which task add dropped silently, so each task had only unit and independent-review, and Genesis has no command to add a gate to an existing task. The owner chose one manual edit, as for M21a: the gate regression, command .venv Scripts python.exe -m pytest -q, mandatory and pending, was inserted after unit in the four tasks in .genesis/project.json; a reserialisation check showed no other change; plan check then passed (32 tasks cover 218 requirements). Lesson: pass --gate and its value as two arguments, and read back every added task gates.

decisions.title: M25a: the W2 window settled before M26, ordered by pausing M26 to M28 (owner)
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-11 after M25 round 1 (KNOWLEDGE-be223191): complete M25, then M25a before M26 as FR-109 and AC-82: an exception raised at the claim-lock wait on a thread is the thread own outcome only when the future is done with that same outcome; anything else is delivered and raised after the cleanup, even when the future completed in the same loop iteration, so no cancellation or timeout is swallowed; FR-99 false sentence corrected. Ordering by CLI with no hand edit: M26 requeued, M26 to M28 paused, plan reopened, M25a added, spec and plan re-signed by the owner; after M25a, M26 to M28 resumed and requeued and the plan re-signed again. KeyFailed cosmetics (__suppress_context__ forced, pickling) stay carried.

decisions.title: M26 pre-flight: a gated node whose signals fire fails criterion_not_available until M27
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-12 at the M26 pre-flight. The critic arrives with M27, so in M26 a gated node whose signals fire records its gate verification with outcome critic_required and GateEvaluated, then fails with criterion_not_available: critic; the critic arrives with M27, the reason a critic criterion gives today; M27 replaces that one branch with the critic run. Clean signals satisfy the criterion with no model call. Interpretation stated for review: a node subject is valid when its plan node is stored for the subject run in the ledger tenant and project and that run is the ledger run or descends from it by parent_run_id, the same rule on both stores (the Runner records each run parent for the in-memory check). The node reservation is held through the gate only for a node that will be gated, so ungated plans keep their budget timing (NFR-29).

decisions.title: M26a: the gate caveats settled before M27 (owner)
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-12 after M26 round 1 (KNOWLEDGE-306e8bfc): complete M26, then M26a before M27 as FR-110 and AC-83. (1) Narrow FR-103 and AC-78 to the model: record_validation is in no tool registry and no shipped tool calls it; a custom tool reaches the Runner through _runner and is first-party in-process code outside the threat model (DECISION-2bad84bb), declared; the test walks scope field values, not names, and runs every shipped tool with record_validation watched. (2) Make 0012 comment true with migration 0013: UNIQUE (claim_id, tenant_id, project_id, ledger_run_id) on claims and a composite foreign key from the verification claim subject, so the schema refuses a cross-tenant or cross-ledger claim row with the store check bypassed; 0012 is not edited because its checksum is recorded. (3) README states the criteria order. (4) low_confidence fires on a claim only a critic contributed to. Ordering by CLI as DECISION-4cf55a17: M27 requeued, M27 and M28 paused, M26a added, spec and plan signed by the owner, and after M26a M27 and M28 resumed and requeued and the plan re-signed.

decisions.title: Gates run in the background with a 25-minute limit from M27 (owner)
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-12 at the M27 pre-flight. Profiled with --durations: the full suite took 6m47s (1989 tests), against 7m15s and 8m06s in the M26 and M26a gate runs, so load explains much of the spread; the 41 tests over one second sum to 159 s (slowest the postgres exit-signal test at 20 s and the two live golden evals at 21 s together), and the remaining 250 s is spread over about 1950 tests at roughly 0.13 s each, most likely per-test database cleanup fixtures. Growth is linear in test count. From M27 on, genesis gate runs in the background with --timeout 1500000, past the 10-minute foreground limit, and each gate time is reported so growth stays visible; per-test overhead is not changed.

decisions.title: M27 caveats settled at M28 pre-flight; an answer-only correction is valid (owner)
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-12 after M27 round 1 (KNOWLEDGE in project.json, M27 round 1): complete M27 and settle its caveats inside M28 pre-flight, reviewed with M28, rather than a separate M27a. A corrected verdict with an empty corrections list is valid: the critic may correct the wording of the answer while every claim stands; the answer carries the taint of both and the verification records no applied corrections; stated in FR-104 and FR-105 and tested. The owner permitted signing the spec and plan changes as siva-rgb (owner).

decisions.title: M28 clarifications of FR-107 and FR-108: outcomes counted, unvalidated claims, example 23 live (owner)
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-10-12 at M28 pre-flight. (1) min_outcomes counts the distinct claims a gate judged that have an external outcome, a claim with several outcomes once by its latest; node outcomes, repeats and unjudged claims do not count. (2) A judged claim with no external outcome is reported in its own no_outcome column of the per-signal counts; the threshold counts and the suggested threshold use only claims with an outcome. (3) Example 23 live runs gateway readers and a real critic, like example 22 live, and checks only what must hold whatever the models decide: at most one critic run per node execution, taint never lowered, every verification in the run tenant and project, and the checks of FR-96; the exact expected set of critic runs is checked offline, where the corpus fixes it. Recorded in FR-107 and FR-108.

decisions.title: Phase 4 P4-D1 to P4-D4: two increments, interruptions recorded now, an approval exit signal, a phase-4 branch (owner)
decisions.text: Owner decisions 2026-10-13, after the RunState study (KNOWLEDGE-5b3b78e5). P4-D1: Phase 4 is specified in two increments, each starting with the items carried into it (M28 review: corrected_answer unguarded, the two report wording items, the NFR-29 test). Increment 1: interruptions, the basic ApprovalManager and Tier 2 write and edit tools behind it. Increment 2: native MCP, the tool catalog (ADR-28), credential brokering (ADR-27) and tenant-scoped skills and instruction bundles; scanning child output for instruction-shaped text is placed when increment 2 is specified. P4-D2: every interruption and every decision is a database row from increment 1, so the record is complete and Phase 6 builds on it; resuming needs the same process, and a paused run whose process ends is recorded as failed. ADR-29 is kept: durable, restart-surviving resume stays Phase 6. P4-D3: increment 1 exit signal is approval under contention: an orchestrated plan whose children call write and edit tools needing approval in parallel, some approved, some rejected, some sticky, one decided twice concurrently, one expired; on both stores each call runs at most once and only when approved, every decision is recorded and bound to its tenant and project, a rejection reaches the model, and nothing runs while paused. P4-D4: Phase 4 is built on a new branch phase-4 from the approved phase-2 tip (8c7345f); phase-2 stays as the record of Phases 2 and 3, and merging into main is a separate owner decision. The publish filter covers main and phase-2 and must be extended before phase-4 is published.

decisions.title: Phase 4 increment 1: deciding, turn shape, sticky decisions and waiting (P4-D5 to P4-D8, owner)
decisions.text: Owner decisions 2026-10-13. P4-D5: an application decides a pending approval through Runner.decide(tenant_id, project_id, interruption_id, approve or reject, principal, message), recorded as a row bound to the tenant, project and deciding principal and usable once, a second decision on the same interruption refused; RunHandle.approve and reject are shortcuts to it. It is never a tool, so no model can approve its own call. P4-D6: in a turn with a call needing approval, the calls needing none run as usual and the model is not called again until every pending call of the turn is decided; an approved call then runs, and a rejected one returns a tool error result, rejected: <message>, so the model can adapt (as OpenAI resolves an interrupted turn, KNOWLEDGE-5b3b78e5). P4-D7: a decision may be sticky for the rest of the run, for one agent and one tool, recorded as its own row naming who made it; an exact per-call decision overrides it, and nothing outlives the run. P4-D8: each interruption has an expiry, a RunConfig field defaulting to one hour; an expired one is recorded and treated as a rejection, approval expired. A waiting child keeps its node budget reservation, waiting charges no tokens, and cancelling the run cancels its pending interruptions, recorded.

decisions.title: Phase 4 increment 1: trigger, Tier 2 tools, orchestration and milestones (P4-D9 to P4-D12, owner)
decisions.text: Owner decisions 2026-10-13. P4-D9: a call needs approval when any of three sources says so: the tool declared ApprovalPolicy (Tier 2 tools default to REQUIRE_APPROVAL), an optional per-tool predicate over the arguments, or a RuntimeHook returning REQUIRE_APPROVAL. It is decided at executor step 4, after permission, so a denied call is never asked about. P4-D10: increment 1 ships write_file, which creates or replaces a file, and edit_file, which replaces one exact, unique string and is refused if it is absent or ambiguous. Both are confined like the M10 file tools, write atomically (a temporary file, then a rename), refuse links and paths outside the root, and put the change and its before and after hashes in the approval request. Delete, move and apply_patch are not in increment 1. P4-D11: an approval needed inside an orchestrated plan is recorded against the child and listed on the top-level run; the child and its node wait while other nodes keep running, the plan settles only when its nodes do, decisions use the interruption id whatever the depth, and the node keeps its reservation (P4-D8). P4-D12: four milestones. M29: the M28 carried items, and the interruption and decision records (a migration) with no behaviour change. M30: the ApprovalManager in single runs, with Runner.decide, sticky decisions and expiry (example 24). M31: write_file and edit_file (example 25). M32: approvals inside orchestration and the exit signal under contention (example 26). Examples run offline on both stores and live.

decisions.title: Phase 4 increment 1 after the spec review: issue order, a stopped paused run, sticky scope (P4-D13 to P4-D15, owner)
decisions.text: Owner decisions 2026-10-13 after the read-only spec review of the first draft (Sonnet 5). P4-D13 refines P4-D6: every call of a turn is prepared and every approval of the turn is asked at once; calls before the first pending call run immediately, and from the first pending call onward the calls run in issue order once every decision is in, an approved call running and a rejected one returning its rejection, so side effects keep the order the model gave. P4-D14 amends P4-D2: an orderly stop of a paused run, by cancellation or shutdown, ends it cancelled with each pending interruption decided cancel, as any cancelled run; after a crash the rows stay as they were, Runner.interruptions marks them as not waiting, and decide refuses them; recovering them is Phase 6. P4-D15 refines P4-D7: a sticky decision, approve or reject, decides every not yet decided call of that agent and tool in the run, siblings pending in the same turn included, but only calls that needed approval because of the tool declared policy; a call flagged by an argument predicate or a hook is always asked; a call already decided keeps its decision.

decisions.title: Phase 4 increment 1: the spec-level choices of the second draft accepted (owner)
decisions.text: Owner accepted on 2026-10-13, after the read-only spec review of the first draft, the nine choices the second draft of FR-111 to FR-121 makes beyond P4-D1 to P4-D15: (1) the interruption is created after before_tool (step 5), not at step 4, so a hook can require approval and the request shows the call as it will run; HALT from before_tool stays ignored; (2) a deciding principal must name a user or a service; (3) every call requiring approval gets an interruption row, one decided by a standing decision included; (4) the waiting run acts only on what the store holds, re-reading on each wake and at least every five seconds; (5) a rejection text is labelled by its decision with the SDK internal trust, since a principal wrote it; (6) a child waiting for approval keeps its concurrency slot; (7) a run top-level run is its ledger_run_id; (8) the write tools refuse a target changed since its request was described or held open by another handle, refuse a target that is itself a link while allowing in-root links in the path, use a withheld temporary file, and declare the window between re-hash and replace; (9) the M28 report items are settled by no_claims_fired and a critic table joined by node execution.

decisions.title: M32 round 1: the exit signal is repaired before increment 1 closes, with a round 2 review (owner)
decisions.text: The owner chose to repair C1 to C8 of the M32 round 1 review before task complete, since P4-D3 makes the exit signal the evidence that Phase 4 increment 1 is finished: the contention bullet requires the race and compares; base.txt edits do not commute and run in one turn; executions are counted at the tool, not by call id; every view decision is guarded so a missing one is a FAIL; the event waits in the gate tests are bounded so a missing emit fails rather than hangs; task_id is asserted on the child own stream; the critic test runs a critic; the sweep matches the exact temporary-file shape of its own target. The owner also chose a conftest guard: a pytest session refuses to start while another holds the session lock on the development database, since reviewers broke the one-session rule at M31 and M32. That edit to an approved file is listed for round 2.

decisions.title: M32 round 3: witnesses on every bullet of the exit signal; example 23 live recorded for the next phase (owner)
decisions.text: The owner chose for round 3: a witness on the rejection bullet (at least one principal rejection, b.txt decided by a principal offline), on the issue-order bullet (some writer with two executions), and on the rest of example 26; the approval screen records its own failures rather than swallowing them, with a check that every decision it meant to make was recorded; a test that a late screen fails the signal; and two small carried items, the guard test without DATABASE_URL and a case-insensitive sweep. Example 23 live unwitnessed bullets are fixed at the next phase pre-flight. AGENTSDK_TEST_SESSION stays unchecked, declared as a guard against accidents in the conftest comment.

decisions.title: Phase 4 increment 2: split, protocol era, transports and features (P4-D16 to P4-D19, owner)
decisions.text: From KNOWLEDGE-07544107, the owner chose on 2026-10-15. P4-D16 Split: increment 2 is native MCP and the tool catalog with snapshots (ADR-28), which the rug-pull defence makes inseparable; credential brokering (ADR-27) and tenant-scoped skills and instruction bundles become a third Phase 4 increment, specified once MCP exists. P4-D17 Era: dual-era, probing server/discover and falling back to the initialize handshake, as the 2026-07-28 spec advises. P4-D18 Transports: stdio and Streamable HTTP; not the deprecated HTTP+SSE. P4-D19 Features: tools (list, call, outputSchema validation, isError, list_changed), input-required results (MRTR) as a RunInterruption kind, elicitation in form and url mode through the interruption path, and resources and prompts.

decisions.title: Phase 4 increment 2: approval, catalog changes, naming and HTTP auth (P4-D20 to P4-D23, owner)
decisions.text: The owner chose on 2026-10-15. P4-D20 Approval: a per-server policy, require by default, never, or per-tool overrides; the approver sees the full arguments; tool annotations never relax approval unless the server is configured as trusted, since the spec makes them untrusted. P4-D21 Catalog changes: catalog snapshots hash each tool description, schema and annotations; a tool whose hash changed is unavailable, with the reason recorded, until the owner accepts the new snapshot, and no standing decision for an old hash carries over. P4-D22 Naming: the qualified name is the configured server alias, two underscores, and the tool name, never serverInfo.name; per server an allow list then a deny list; agent tool profiles name qualified tools. P4-D23 HTTP auth: static configured headers for Streamable HTTP and environment variables for stdio, never in model context or stored rows; no OAuth client until the credential broker increment.

decisions.title: Phase 4 increment 2: dependency, server launch, exit signal and milestones (P4-D24 to P4-D27, owner)
decisions.text: The owner chose on 2026-10-15. P4-D24 Dependency: the mcp library is an optional extra, agentsdk[mcp], pinned mcp==2.3.0; the core still imports without it (NFR-6), and the MCP module raises a clear error when the extra is missing; NFR-9 is amended accordingly. P4-D25 Launch: MCP servers come only from code-level configuration, never from a model or a file found at run time; the exact command, arguments and the names (not values) of environment variables are recorded in the ExecutionManifest; no sandbox before Phase 5. P4-D26 Exit signal: hostile servers under orchestration: a plan of children using real local MCP servers over stdio and Streamable HTTP, one changing a tool mid-run, one with a poisoned description, one shadowing another server tool name, one returning injection text and one asking for input; the change is blocked, names never collide, every result is untrusted, approvals and input-required are honoured, on both stores, ten times. P4-D27 Milestones: five. M33: the pre-flight (the M32 and example 23 carried items) and the stdio client, dual era, tools, naming, filtering and provenance. M34: catalog snapshots, the approval policy and blocking a changed tool. M35: Streamable HTTP with configured headers, and resources and prompts. M36: input-required results and elicitation as interruptions. M37: the exit signal.

decisions.title: Phase 4 increment 2 after the spec review: connections, first sight, visibility and acceptance (P4-D28 to P4-D31, owner)
decisions.text: After a read-only review of the first draft, the owner chose on 2026-10-18. P4-D28 Connection scope: one connection per server alias, tenant and project in a Runner, shared by that tenancy runs on one event loop; no server-side state crosses tenants; a crash restarts the connection once per connection lifetime. P4-D29 First sight: a tool seen for the first time is unusable until its hash is accepted, as a changed one is. P4-D30 Who is sent MCP tools: only agents whose tool_profile names the qualified tool or the alias wildcard, in every run whether or not it carries a ContextPolicy; built-in and application tools keep DECISION-ca1ad3e0. P4-D31 Acceptance: any user or service principal accepts per tool hash, per tenant and project; acceptance in code names its tenant, project and service principal in the server config. The drafter also splits the schema changes by milestone: 0016 at M33, 0017 at M34, 0018 at M36.

decisions.title: Phase 4 increment 2: the ten spec-level choices of the second draft accepted (owner)
decisions.text: On 2026-10-18 the owner accepted the ten choices the second draft of the Phase 4 increment 2 specification makes beyond P4-D16 to P4-D31, as listed in SPEC.md open questions under Second draft 2026-10-18: results untrusted even from a trusted server; untrusted tools destructive and sequential, trusted annotations mapped, by_annotations for trusted servers only; qualified names within A-Za-z0-9_- up to 64 with skips for duplicates and clashes; MCP tools never registered, each turn rebuilt, Runner gains aclose; no executor deadline on MCP tools, each round trip timed; resources and prompts read by the application through tenancy-scoped Runner methods, offered to the model only with resources_as_tool, versioned and accepted; input requests waited inside step 6, answered by Runner.respond and RunHandle.respond, sampling and roots unsupported, at most three input rounds under the original approval; migrations 0016, 0017 and 0018 by milestone; a url-mode URL stored whole with a README warning; the carried caveats as FR-122 states. The owner asked to sign and move to the plan.

decisions.title: M33 round 2: every wait on a server bounded, the wildcard guarded, two caveats settled (owner)
decisions.text: The owner chose for M33 round 2: bound every await on server-controlled input, not only the two sites found: a connect_timeout on StdioServer (default 30 s) over the start, the discover or initialize exchange and the whole listing; the listing capped by pages as well as tools; calls already bounded by call_timeout; closing a connection bounded; each wait tested with a server that starts but never answers (a banner then silence, reads but never replies, endless empty pages, ignores the end of its input). The srv__* wildcard allows only names with a tool part after the separator. The inherited environment (the library twelve names) is declared in the README, and the output-error mapping is pinned by a test that fails if the library message changes.

decisions.title: M33 round 3: an SDK-owned deadline on every call, a wedged connection discarded, aclose final, stall dumps of asyncio tasks (owner)
decisions.text: The owner chose for M33 round 3: every MCP call runs under the SDK own asyncio deadline, call_timeout plus one second, so the library read timeout still decides a slow honest tool; when the SDK deadline fires first the request write was blocked and the stream may hold half a message, so that connection is ended, the call fails ToolTimeout, and the next call restarts it under the restart-once rule. aclose marks the Runner loop closed, so no connection reopens on it. Tested structurally: after a wedged write every later call returns within its bound (70 KB and 2 MB), and a run in flight across aclose starts no server. faulthandler_timeout stays, and a conftest watchdog prints every asyncio task stack of the running loop on the same timeout, listed for review as an edit to conftest.py.

decisions.title: M33 round 4: one lifecycle gate made final under one lock, sessions owned by their calls, every loop closed (owner)
decisions.text: The owner asked that the repeated rejections be fixed carefully so the next round passes. Round 4 redesigns the connection lifecycle rather than patching a site: ensure is the only place a server starts and checks closed under the connection lock; close sets closed and takes the same lock, so a start in progress finishes and is then ended and nothing starts after; McpClients.aclose closes the Runner to MCP for good, on every event loop, closing connections of other running loops on their own loop; a call captures its own session (client and task) and a discard ends only that session; the serve task unsets the client only while it is the current session; the wedge margin is 5 s past call_timeout. Tests cover every holder: a retained tool and a retained connection after aclose, aclose during a connect, a stale session ending after a restart, an honest slow tool keeping its connection, and a run on another loop. Before review, a fresh agent attacks the lifecycle adversarially with runtime probes.

decisions.title: M33 round 4: server regexes validated in a process of their own (owner), and the clarifications the redesign makes
decisions.text: A third pre-review found that a server schema pattern ran in this process, and Python re holds the GIL, so a catastrophic one froze every thread past every SDK bound, refuting the spec risk entry that worker-thread validation contains it. The owner chose validation in a subprocess: a schema carrying pattern or patternProperties is validated, input by the executor and output through the session validation hook, in a short-lived process of the real interpreter ended at 10 s; any other schema is validated in process, since without a regular expression validation cannot stall. Clarifications of the signed spec, for review: (1) FR-124 says a run on another loop opens its own connection; the round 4 design keeps all of a Runner connections on one private event loop on its own thread, which P4-D28 (one event loop per connection) still describes, and which removes every loop-affinity defect the pre-reviews found; (2) FR-123 and AC-90 name UnknownMcpServer for Runner.accept_tools, respond and the mcp_ methods, which arrive with M34 to M36, so the type arrives with them; (3) the <alias>__* wildcard is the MCP view: a run with servers wraps its default allowlist so the wildcard allows only a configured server tools, and runs without MCP are unchanged (NFR-38); (4) a restart a call makes reports its events at the next refresh.

decisions.title: M33 round 5: no server schema is ever evaluated in process, and the bounds are checked by tests (owner)
decisions.text: Following the round 4 rejection and the owner instruction to fix the family at its root: every evaluation against a server-supplied schema -- the model arguments, the server results, and the listing schema checks, one batch per listing -- runs in a short-lived process of the real interpreter ended at 10 s; the regular-expression distinction is removed, since deep anyOf with none is exponential too. Two tests make the invariant checkable: a runtime test patches jsonschema in the test process during a run of MCP tools and fails if any schema other than JSON Schema own metaschemas is evaluated there; a static test walks agentsdk/mcp, requires every await, async with and blocking call to appear in a table naming its bound, and every subprocess call to carry a timeout, failing on an unlisted wait or a stale entry.

decisions.title: M33 round 6: every guard an asserted property, every earlier finding answered (author choices, for the owner to confirm; re-recorded)
decisions.text: First recorded as DECISION-e8746c66 on 2026-10-19 during a gate run, whose write-back of project.json lost it; the round 6 brief cites that id. After round 5 was rejected for the alias wildcard, which round 4 had named and round 5 dropped, round 6 makes four choices the owner has not yet ruled on. ONE, the wildcard: <alias>__* allows a call only when the tool the run executes under that name is the very object a connection built from its server listing, read from the run own view; never by name shape. TWO, one entry the SDK reads never fails its server: an entry the SDK cannot store or build, an empty name, or an invalid output schema is skipped with its reason; entries the mcp library itself refuses still refuse the whole listing, as declared. THREE, the listing is checked 50 tools to a process, up to twenty side by side within the one 10 s deadline, and a chunk that cannot be checked has all its tools skipped. FOUR, every failure of an MCP tool, before it ran too, carries the tool declared untrusted provenance, since its schemas are the server text. Also: McpServerUnavailable is asserted of the outcome, once a run; the static bounds tests are inverted with a test of the test; aclose returns once the engine thread has ended. Process: the repair brief carries a ledger of every finding and caveat of all earlier rejections, and a missing or false row is itself a finding.

knowledge.title: Gateway fronts 308 models across four providers
knowledge.text: GET /models (not /v1/models, which Envoy blocks with 'fault filter abort' 403) lists 308 model ids namespaced by provider: bedrock.*, azure.*, openai.*, vertex_ai.*. Tool calling verified working on both openai.gpt-4o-mini and bedrock.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5 through the identical OpenAI-shaped request, so provider switching in Phase 0 is a model-id change rather than an adapter change.

knowledge.title: Genesis gate commands must use Windows path separators
knowledge.text: genesis.mjs executes gate commands through cmd.exe on win32. A command beginning with a forward-slash path such as .venv/Scripts/python.exe fails with "'.venv' is not recognized" because cmd parses /Scripts as a switch. Gate commands on this host must be written .venv\Scripts\python.exe.
