The M13 ArtifactStore protocol with its in-memory and Postgres implementations is the pattern for the plan store. InvalidStructuredOutput exists in errors.py, unused since Phase 0, for M18. Two spec gaps were found and decided by the owner as DECISION-8f8cc54c.

knowledge.title: M16 round 2: F1, F3 and F5 verified fixed; follow-ups G1 and G3
knowledge.text: Round 2, Sonnet 5 in a fresh session, approved at 2026-09-19T17:06:04Z with no blocking finding, on source hash 8f5e56d9 with unit 142 and regression 1375. The owner verified it first-hand. F3: the round 1 probe p02_hash reports no Postgres failures across 115 checks, and its tamper step now raises PlanIntegrityError. F1: every check of the owning tenant side passes in p01_scope; its remaining FAIL lines expect another tenant reusing a plan id to be refused, whereas under scoped identity that is the other tenant own plan and reveals nothing. The rewrite of migration 0007 and the reset left the development database consistent: the recorded checksum matches the file, document is text, both primary keys lead with tenant_id and project_id, the remaining demo plan rows hash correctly from their stored text, and no plan row points at a missing run or version. Follow-ups, none blocking. G1: the duplicate node id check in plan.py counts each id in a list, so it grows with the square of the plan size, about 2 s at 16000 nodes; max_tasks_per_run is 50 by default, so fix it only if large plans become possible, with a Counter. G2 is F4, already carried to M19 with F2 by DECISION-6d073ac0. G3: round 1 probes p02_hash, p07_residue and p08_demo still assume a JSONB document and now print false FAIL lines; they are review scratch, not part of the repository, so update them before rerunning them.

knowledge.title: M17 pre-flight: baseline, what the budget governor touches, and the prices found
knowledge.text: Baseline at 7d9e485 with no other python or node process: 1375 passed in 233.16 s, peak suite footprint 32 MB, no test past 120 s. Code facts: ModelPricing in registry.py holds Decimal USD per token for input, output, cache_read and cache_write, and call_cost prices one call, returning None rather than 0 when a used class has no price. A run price comes only from a caller-supplied ModelRegistry entry, entry.capabilities.pricing, read in Runner._cost and recorded in the manifest pricing column; the registry ships none. The per-run meter in loop.py sums call costs. The agent loop already calls control.checkpoint before each model call, the natural place for a lease check. BudgetExceeded, MaxDepthExceeded, DependencyFailed and ReplanLimitExceeded exist in errors.py as unused Phase 0 placeholders under WorkflowError. PlanNode.budget_reservation from M16 carries an optional Decimal usd and an optional int tokens. Migration checksums are newline-normalised, so a CRLF checkout does not break them. Prices fetched on 2026-09-19 from official pages: Anthropic, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, Claude Haiku 4.5 at 1 USD per million input tokens, 5 output, 0.10 cache hits, 1.25 for 5 minute cache writes; OpenAI, https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, gpt-4o-mini at 0.15 input, 0.075 cached input, 0.60 output; neither page carries a date. The Anthropic page says Amazon Bedrock sets its own prices and that its regional endpoints for Haiku 4.5 carry a 10 percent premium over global ones; the AWS Bedrock pricing page reset the connection twice and was not read, and which endpoint type the gateway uses is not visible from here. So the list price for bedrock.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5 is unverified, and M15 costed that model at the Anthropic first-party rate: if the gateway routes to a regional endpoint, both M15 arms were understated by 10 percent, with their ratio unchanged.

knowledge.title: M17 round 5 approved after four rejections; K1 to K8 carried forward
knowledge.text: Round 5, Fable 5.1 in a fresh session, approved at 2026-09-25T16:01:27Z with no blocking finding, on source hash d286b198 with unit 89 and regression 1464, and the owner verified it. J1 was checked with round 4 own probe: the duplicate terminal event is gone, one RunCompleted remains, and the caller still hears the store failure through a FAILED result carrying the error. The runs row stays running in that case by design: M4 contract says a failed status write is reported rather than swallowed, and NFR-17 conditions no run left running on the store accepting the terminal write, so the reviewer concluded M4 and FR-31 do not conflict. Coverage was 42 runs across 6 store failure seams by 7 endings, 800 random splits, concurrency under a barrier, and the pricing page fetched and quoted; 12 reviewer mutants all killed, including one proving that keying the skip on terminal rather than terminal_written breaks the M9 R2 sweep. Caveats recorded for later, none blocking. K1: terminal_written is set only on the completion path, so after a cancellation or an exception the flag is False although a terminal event was written; nothing reads it there today, but the docstring in handle.py claims more than the code does. K3: top_up accepts a negative amount and moves money back out of a node reservation, although its docstring says top-ups are sign checked. K4: a negative total_tokens with positive parts charges 0 tokens while the call is still priced. K5: a usage object that is not a Usage leaves the manifest tokens disagreeing with the run. K6: reservations are recorded at start only, so a later top-up is not reflected in the manifest. K7: extreme USD ceilings. K8: a junk budget_lease fails with AttributeError rather than a named validation error. K1 and K3 are worth fixing before M18 or M19 builds on the governor.

knowledge.title: M18 pre-flight: K1 and K3 fixed, baseline, and what subagents build on
knowledge.text: The two carried caveats were fixed first, as DECISION-21e5d2e9 directed. K3: BudgetGovernor.top_up now refuses an amount that is not positive in whichever units it sets, because a BudgetAmount records whatever it is given since H1 relaxed it, so an unchecked top-up could take money back out of a node through a method that only claims to add; a test drives negative usd, negative tokens, a mixed amount and zero in either unit, and checks nothing moved. K1: RunControl.terminal_written was set on the completion path only, so after a cancellation or a failure handled outside the loop it read False although a terminal event had been written; it is now set wherever a terminal event is written, and a test asserts it for a completed, a failed and a cancelled run. Baseline after both, at 4cfb054 with those fixes applied and no other python or node process: 1468 passed in 333.20 s, peak suite footprint 32 MB, lowest free memory 441 MB, no test past 120 s. Code facts for M18: runs.parent_run_id exists from migration 0002 and RunConfig.parent_run_id is validated when the config is built, as scripts/07 shows; ContentProvenance.from_model is the ADR-26 rule, taking the union of its inputs taint and the least trusting zone; ModelRequest.output_schema exists and is always None today, set at one call site in ContextAssembler.build; InvalidStructuredOutput, MaxDepthExceeded, DependencyFailed and ReplanLimitExceeded are unused Phase 0 placeholders under WorkflowError; SchedulerLimits holds max_concurrent_tools and the two mappings and will gain three fields; the loop returns its answer at the point where a response carries no tool calls, which is where the FR-71 validation belongs; InMemoryArtifactStore and the Postgres one resolve an input ref within one tenant and project. Four specification gaps were found and decided by the owner as DECISION-35f4c3f4. One reading is recorded here rather than put to the owner: FR-72 says a run past max_tasks_per_run refuses the spawn the same way, and the sentence before it names MaxDepthExceeded, so the same error is raised for both, with the message naming which limit was reached.

knowledge.title: M18a pre-flight: baseline, the checkout sites, and where briefed-input provenance has to travel
knowledge.text: Baseline at 252c51a, clean tree, no other python or node process: 1504 passed in 283.97 s with -p no:cacheprovider. Code facts: postgres.py has 19 connection checkouts, every one written as _pool(self._dsn).connection() inside a synchronous store method, and no other module checks out from the pool; apply_schema and migrate use psycopg.connect directly and run before any loop. The async artifact and run-state methods already offload through asyncio.to_thread. ContextAssembler.build assembles request metadata provenance only from tool results in the history; providers never read ModelRequest.metadata, so an entry there reaches no prompt. The child task is one string built by SubagentPool._brief and stored as the run first user message, so FR-84 marker is visible in stored history; a briefed input reaches the child loop through nothing but that string, so FR-83 needs a channel from the pool to the assembler. RunConfig.depth defaults to 0 and nothing reads it (D11); FR-79 and AC-64 refuse 0, resolved by the owner. ContentProvenance.from_model always yields origin model and authority advisory, so the demo injected-instruction check can assert trust zone and taint, not authority. The existing thread-identity test monkeypatches postgres._pool through the test monkeypatch fixture and calls undo, so an autouse wrapper must use its own MonkeyPatch to survive it.

knowledge.title: M18a round 1 approved; six caveats carried forward
knowledge.text: Sonnet 5 approved M18a-validation-and-guard in round 1 at 2026-10-07T08:52:32Z (control 98d3eb3b) on source hash d5c75afd, the hash of both passing gates; the first approval in the M18 chain. The owner confirmed C4 itself rather than a proxy: with the to_thread removed from the Postgres artifact read used by _brief, the M18 enumeration test still passed while FR-82 refused at the checkout and FR-81 failed the test at teardown, independently. Owner scans: the only .connection( in agentsdk is inside _checkout, no getconn anywhere; the fixture has no marker, path list, name filter or skip. Caveats carried forward, none blocking: (1) migrate.py is the only Postgres I/O neither guard watches; literally compliant, since FR-82 governs store calls and migration is schema setup, but Persistence.postgres built from inside a coroutine runs apply_schema on the loop unwatched; a one-time startup cost, owner-highlighted. (2) A refused terminal write leaves the run row running, byte for byte what an ordinary database failure at that write already does through the swallow in _safe_finish; reachable only if the terminal write is un-offloaded, which the fixture now catches; the running-row gap in _safe_finish is pre-existing, open, and not M18a work; owner-highlighted. (3) A test that replaces postgres._pool with an unwatched pool and swallows the refusal would evade FR-81; no existing test does, and the four that patch _pool capture the watched pool. (4) The logs-once set _LOGGED is unlocked, so concurrent first violations may log twice. (5) The example check labelled_like_the_note duplicates the taint check before it. (6) Custom assemblers now always receive briefed_inputs as a keyword.

knowledge.title: M19 pre-flight: baseline, what M19 owes from earlier milestones, and the readings taken
knowledge.text: Baseline at 7af8202 with only Genesis records changed, no other python or node process: 1539 passed in 283.68 s with -p no:cacheprovider. Owed before anything drives nodes (DECISION-6d073ac0): F2, a RunStateStore transition accepts any event sink, so a node event can land in another run; F4, on Postgres the row lock ends at commit before the emit, so two racing transitions of one node can record Finished before Started. Reachable now and owed: the M18 round 3 note that a tool wrapping a nested spawn cannot pass the grandchild real provenance, which FR-76 makes reachable; D11, RunConfig.depth read by nothing until M19. Carried and not in scope unless touched: G1 (quadratic duplicate node check, harmless under max_tasks_per_run 50), K2 and K4 to K8 (KNOWLEDGE-fdff16dc), M18 M3 to M8, M18a caveats (KNOWLEDGE-8bde2cc5), the ADR-12 harness follow-ups (DECISION-750df4c4, which belong to the eval harness, not M19). Code facts: BudgetGovernor(policy, plan) splits once per plan and has orchestrator_lease and top_up; BudgetPolicy.max_replans defaults to 3; AcceptanceCriterion stores kind, target, arguments, description, with artifact_exists naming an artifact uri in target; PlanNode stores timeout and retry_policy with no behaviour yet; EventType has PLAN_NODE_STARTED and PLAN_NODE_FINISHED, emitted by emit_transition through a sink the caller passes; the executor calls tools as tool.fn(**arguments); RunScope is a frozen postgres.RunScope of run_id, tenant_id and project_id. Readings taken here rather than put to the owner, stated in the review prompt: a node assigned_role resolves through a roles mapping given to the orchestrator, an unknown role failing the node; artifact_exists passes when the named uri exists in the run scope, was written by that node, and reads back verifying its content_hash (FR-55), so a mismatched hash is a tampered artifact; timeout and retry_policy keep their stored shape and gain no behaviour in M19, because FR-73 to FR-76 give them none; FR-76 extends RunScope with an optional node_id and artifact store rather than adding a second type of the same name.

knowledge.title: A test that fixes the schedule cannot see the race it is for
knowledge.text: M19 round 4: the D6 test parked both sibling tasks behind a barrier until both had returned, so asyncio.wait always handed back two finished tasks and the in-flight case the defect lived in could never occur; the test passed while the reviewer's probe reproduced the defect 5 of 6 times. A test for a property of concurrent code must not choose which tasks are in flight. Either hold the exact case deterministically at a point that leaves it in flight (here: after the child's tool ran, at the output write), or run the unheld shape repeatedly, and prefer both. Write the test to the property (a node whose tool ran is never rerun), not to the repair (harvest what returned).

knowledge.title: M19 round 5 approved after four rejections; caveats carried forward
knowledge.text: Approved 13:07:29Z by Sonnet 5 (fallback for Fable 5.1) on source hash 6871154d: unit 51 passed, regression 1590 passed, 43 of 43 author mutants killed. The reviewer's own D6 probe ran clean 20 of 20 and, with the wait removed, reproduced 9 of 12, so the negative is meaningful. Coverage note: the approval rests partly on carry-over. Round 5 did not re-probe budget/USD, FR-76 attribution or the Postgres half of F2/F4 first-hand; the owner accepted that because budget.py, executor.py, scope.py, tools.py, plan.py and postgres.py are byte-identical to what round 4 (Opus 5) verified first-hand, and taint was checked again because orchestrator.py changed. Non-blocking caveats carried forward: (1) _with_scope matches the annotation by literal name, so a tool declaring RunScope | None, an alias or a subclass receives no scope, against FR-76; (2) a criterion whose own check raises is reported node_error rather than naming the criterion, against FR-74; (3) _check's emit closure ignores its event_type; (4) node rows of an abandoned version can be left running or pending, judged in round 4 the least false option, since cancelled is final and asserts the node did not run; (5) from DECISION-aab73fd5: ToolScope._runner gives any scoped tool the Runner, so it can reach any tenant's artifact store and set _control.failure (D13, in-process, but wider than NFR-2 suggests), and AttributedArtifacts scopes writes, not reads or deletes; (6) pending_failure is caller-settable, and a hand-built RunConfig without it can end completed with no plan. Label note: the reviewer called the round 4 finding D7; DECISION-9a55c8c7 records it as D6 repaired a second time.

knowledge.title: M20 pre-flight: baseline, what context policy and compaction touch, and the readings taken
knowledge.text: Baseline on HEAD bf7d0d5 (M19): full suite 1590 passed in 307.46s, nothing else running. What M20 touches: loop.py sends self._registry.schemas() every turn (all registered tools, DECISION-ca1ad3e0) and the executor resolves against the whole registry, ToolNotFound at the resolve step; api.py builds the manifest with tool_spec_hashes of every registered spec; manifest.py has no field for what was sent; migrations end at 0008; ModelRegistry knows max_context_tokens for openai.gpt-4o-mini (128000) and bedrock claude-haiku-4-5 (200000) only; Message has no provenance field (only ToolResult does), so a summary's taint cannot ride on the message itself; ContextAssembler already lists briefed inputs and tool results in request metadata provenance (FR-83). Readings taken, not put to the owner: (a) a call to a tool outside a policy run's visible set is refused ToolNotFound, because that run's executor resolves against the filtered view, exactly as an unknown tool is; (b) migration 0009 adds execution_manifests.tools_sent (JSONB, NULL before it): the sorted name and schema_hash of each tool the policy sends, with the registered name as the qualified name until Phase 4 brings namespaces; tool_spec_hashes is unchanged; a before_model hook that rewrites a request's tools is outside what the manifest records, declared; (c) the briefing rules of _brief move into ContextPolicy unchanged, so FR-70's selection is read in one type; (d) the summarising call uses the run's own model and passes the same budget check, is charged to the agent's lease and emits ModelCalled, so a run's usage still equals the sum of its ModelCalled events (NFR-17); ContextCompacted carries the replaced-content artifact, the summary's provenance, the token counts before and after and that call's turn and provider_response_id; (e) the summary's provenance is ContentProvenance.taking_in over every replaced tool result and briefed input, so it never lowers taint; (f) a compaction whose summarising call fails or is refused by the budget ends the run failed, with the reason, rather than continuing toward an overflow; (g) example 18 is added to EXPECTED_EXAMPLES in test_distribution, as every example milestone has.

knowledge.title: M20 round 1 approved; caveats carried forward
knowledge.text: Approved 15:53:59Z by Opus 5 (fallback for Fable 5.1) on source hash eae1be3a: unit 42 passed, regression 1632 passed, the gate evidence recomputed by the reviewer; author mutation run 33 of 33. All seven attack items probed first-hand. A plain run's requests, events and stored messages were byte-identical to HEAD bf7d0d5's in an exported tree (NFR-12). A schedule-independent taint fuzzer found 0 failures in 394 compactions across 104 runs on both stores, and killed 10 of 10 of its own mutants. An invisible tool's refusal is byte-identical to an unknown tool's, ToolCalled payload included, and a before_model hook restoring the schemas cannot restore execution. Caveats carried, not repaired: (C1) ContextCompacted tokens_before is the deciding measure (reported prompt_tokens plus an estimate of what was added) while tokens_after is a fresh whole-view estimate, so the pair can read backwards (108 of 330 fuzzed compactions) although the prompt shrank every time; record both on one basis or label the bases. (C3) a compaction is written before it is recorded (artifact, then summary message, then the event), so a failed emit leaves a summary in messages with no ContextCompacted; the run still ends terminal with the reason; M19 F4 moved the plan-transition emit inside the transaction for the same reason. (C4) tools_sent is written at run start, so a run refused before its first request records a set it never sent. (C5) visibility follows tool_profile, not a custom permission_policy. (C6) under the Orchestrator's default ContextPolicy, a child on a model outside the ModelRegistry is refused at spawn, surfacing as node_error at execution rather than at configuration: a behaviour change for any application using Orchestrator with unregistered models. M20 closes Phase 2's second increment.

knowledge.title: M20a pre-flight: baseline, how the two compaction writes are made today, and the readings taken
knowledge.text: Baseline on HEAD a576adc plus the M20a specification (uncommitted SPEC.md and .genesis): full suite 1632 passed in 238.24s, nothing else running. Today loop._compact writes the artifact, appends the summary through the session store (PostgresSessionStore.append: own checkout and transaction, the messages advisory lock, sequence_no from the stored max) and then emits ContextCompacted through the run's sink (a PublishingSink over PostgresEventStore.emit: another checkout and transaction, the events advisory lock, then the in-process buffer and the RunHandle stream fed after the commit). M19's F4 emits inside the transition's transaction scope through the sink's own connection, so a failed emit rolls the status back, but the two are not one database transaction. Readings taken, not put to the owner: (a) FR-86 is met with one database transaction, stronger than F4's shape: the message insert and the event insert are factored out of append and emit as helpers taking a connection, and a new store write takes both advisory locks in a fixed order (messages, then events) and inserts both on one connection; (b) the stored event then reaches the sink's buffer and the RunHandle stream through a new sink method that records an already-stored event, so RunResult.events and events() stay in sequence_no order; (c) the in-memory stores keep the same rule: the event is built and validated before anything is appended, and a failure after the append removes it, so neither is left; (d) the combined write is an optional extension of the SessionStore protocol (NFR-7): a store without it falls back to append then emit, declared as a limitation for custom stores; (e) FR-85: tokens_before becomes the whole-request estimate of the view before the compaction, on the same basis as tokens_after, and the deciding number moves to threshold_measure with threshold_basis 'reported_plus_estimate' or 'estimate'; the M20 test asserting tokens_after < tokens_before stays true where the summary is shorter than what it replaced, which the AC-68 fuzz checks rather than assumes; (f) the payload keys tokens_before and tokens_after keep their names, so no consumer breaks; their meaning changes and is recorded.

knowledge.title: M20a round 1 approved; F1 and F2 carried to the start of Phase 3
knowledge.text: Approved 06:05:54Z by Fable 5.1 (its first successful start after failing five rounds) on source hash f19dc611: unit 15 passed, regression 1647 passed, the gate evidence recomputed by the reviewer; author mutation run 12 of 12. Verified first-hand: every write point of append_with_event failed on Postgres, the commit included (backend terminated from another connection, AdminShutdown with both rows written, rollback left neither); no deadlock across ten rounds of appenders, emitters, combined writers and a run-row updater, with a detector shown (an opposite-order writer deadlocked 5 of 5) and a lock audit (append_with_event is the only transaction holding two run-scoped locks); FR-85's pair recomputed across 530 compactions on both stores, 472 reported_plus_estimate and 58 estimate, 0 failures; the in-memory take-back is identity-based. The owner chose to complete M20a and carry, not repair: (F1) InMemorySessionStore.append_with_event reads getattr(sink, 'scope', default)[2], but PublishingSink.scope always exists and is None over a scope-less sink, so a run with a scope-less custom sink, which completed under M20, now fails with TypeError: a regression M20a introduced, fail-closed, reachable only with a custom sink. The repair is to skip the check when the sink has no scope, as before M20a; refuse_foreign_sink's shape would refuse it instead. (F2) the in-memory check compares the run id only and accepts a sink for another tenant with the same run id; InMemorySessionStore is shared across runs and never knows a run's tenant, so the full triple needs the tenant passed in; Postgres already compares the triple. Also carried: an artifact with no compaction and a ModelCalled {purpose: compaction} remain after a failed combined write (the second is a true record of a charged call); stored() failing after the commit would split the database from the in-process view (a list insert under a lock); tokens_before changed meaning under the same key for any external consumer of M20's payload; 11 of 530 fuzzed compactions enlarged the history, all with a constant large provider count on a two-message middle, and split() returns None when nothing is left, so no compaction loop forms; and M20's C4 to C6 (KNOWLEDGE-cc4d686c).

knowledge.title: Facts the Phase 3 increment 1 spec review measured in the code, and what the draft changed
knowledge.text: Read-only review on 2026-10-10 by an independent Sonnet reviewer of the first draft of FR-87 to FR-96. Measured: ToolSpec.schema_hash includes configuration whenever it is non-empty, and the fetch tool's configuration always is (allowlist, max_bytes, timeout_seconds, max_redirects), so a new configuration key moves every fetch tool's hash unless it enters only when non-default; _with_scope injects a scope by annotation and returns the arguments unchanged when there is no scope, so a fetch needs a no-scope path; ToolScope carries no briefed inputs, history, parent or root run id, and history is reachable only through Runner._history_for; ToolOutput.source_uri becomes source_uri_or_hash, and four tests (tests/test_builtin_tools.py lines 391, 1782, 2117, 2265) assert FR-38's final-URL source; _fetch_hops returns non-2xx responses as ordinary results; artifacts can expire or be deleted; existing advisory locks are transaction-scoped in spaces 1 and 2, the pool is capped at 32, and store calls run on shielded worker threads, so a blocking lock wait would ignore cancellation; the in-memory session store keys history by run id alone, so two tenants with one run id share a history; EventType is a closed enum. Blocking findings, each repaired in the second draft: B1 a claim's contributor inputs were unreachable from a tool (now readable through the run scope; same-batch siblings excluded, declared); B2 immutable claim rows could not hold a union of contributions (sources and provenance now derived from append-only contributions); B3 a lock keyed by URL alone let one tenant wait for and take another's version (the key now includes the reach); B4 a TENANT hit from another project was uncitable and the PUBLIC_GLOBAL copy needed a stated cross-tenant read (every hit outside the reader's tenant and project is copied, the copy reveals none of the origin's identifiers, and PUBLIC_GLOBAL requires no auth); B5 the claim that a default fetch's schema is unchanged was false (cache settings enter configuration only when non-default); B6 FR-91 silently changed FR-38 (now stated as superseding it, with the four tests listed, and a fetch with no scope keeps the old source). Spec-level choices the second draft makes beyond P3-D1 to P3-D12, for the owner's approval: copy on every hit outside the reader's tenant and project; dedup against active claims only; a supersession onto another active statement refused; non-2xx responses never cached; session-level advisory locks waited on by polling, full jitter, the waiters failing with the last holder rather than retrying; the event names SourceFetched, SourceServed, ClaimRecorded and ClaimSuperseded with stated fields; the in-memory session store keyed by tenant, project and run.

knowledge.title: M21 round 2 approved; four in-memory and sink caveats carried
knowledge.text: Approved 10:42:58Z by Fable 5.1 on source hash 1c386e0f: unit 18 passed, regression 1665 passed, the gate evidence recomputed by the reviewer; author mutation run 13 of 13. Round 1 (Sonnet 5) had rejected on unbound in-memory calls raising under concurrency (DECISION-f12abafb); the lock and run index repair held 0 of 8 at a 1 microsecond switch interval, with a control (the pre-repair scan restored) raising 8 of 8, and the reviewer showed its own detector caught the restored scan 8 of 8 at 1 microsecond but 1 of 8 at the default 5 ms. One non-reentrant lock, every acquisition a leaf, no lock held across a sink's emit, the run index written in one place with zero drift. Round 1's declared gaps were covered: Postgres-backed orchestration with a replan, the C6 replan refusal on Postgres, and all 47 unbound call sites (42 in the suite, 5 in scripts 02, 03, 04, 06 and 10, run offline). Carried, not repaired: (1) InMemorySessionStore.append_with_event derives the key twice on the unbound path, so an unbound combined write racing a run's first bound write can file the message under the bound key while the take-back searches the other, leaving the run id under two keys -- silent wrong state, reachable only by that race, which nothing performs; (2) an unbound append into a Runner's own run id before the Runner's first bound write files it under (None, None, run_id), and later unbound reads of that id are refused as existing in more than one tenant, where HEAD merged them -- loud, names the remedy, the reverse order works, and all 47 unbound call sites are reads; (3) inside a bound combined write, a sink that writes a different run is refused; (4) Postgres keeps no take-back for a failing scope-less sink, as declared. The owner may fold (1) and (2) into M22, which adds stores of its own.

knowledge.title: M21a round 1 approved; three wording and reach caveats carried to M22's pre-flight
knowledge.text: Approved by Opus 5 on source hash 8ade0977, the gates recomputed by the reviewer (regression 1675 passed in 279.87s, observed 12:38:24Z, now the recorded evidence); author mutation run 9 of 9. The reviewer reproduced caveat 2 on the repaired tree (adoption, a second tenant keeping its own history, the ambiguous unbound read still refused), ran 2800 contended attempts at a 1 microsecond switch interval checking the _runs and _by_run invariant after each, with adopters split 141 to 259 and the declared refusal hit, and showed the switch-interval trap on this repair (54 violations at 1 microsecond against the take-back mutant, 0 at 5 ms). Caveat 3 verified by instrumenting AgentLoop.__init__ (4 loops built, 4 seen, scopes agreeing). The manual project.json edit was audited as limited to DECISION-23ae5809. Carried to M22's pre-flight, not repaired: (C1) the README row for caveat 4 says a custom sink that names no scope, but Postgres takes the two-write path for any sink lacking write and stored, including one naming this run correctly; the postgres.py docstring is accurate, the README row narrower; (C2) an unbound in-memory combined write compares only the run id against a scoped sink, so with adoption the summary can land in one tenant's history while the event goes to the sink's tenant, reachable only by code driving AgentLoop directly; (C4) AC-75 says an unbound append before a Runner's first write, which the API cannot deliver because _open draws the run id from uuid4; the gate models it with store.bind(scope).append, which is what api.py hands the loop, verified equivalent by the reviewer.

knowledge.title: M22 round 1 approved; six caveats to settle at M23's pre-flight
knowledge.text: Approved 16:46:05Z by Fable 5.1 on source hash eeb7c464, gates recomputed by the reviewer; author mutation run 24 of 24. The reviewer proved the tenancy rule equivalent across its two implementations: 112 versions over every scope, tenant, project and ledger combination, the SQL reachable, InMemoryEvidenceStore and reaches() compared against an oracle written from FR-90, 48 reader and key checks, zero mismatches, zero leaks, each SQL clause and the Python rule killed by its own mutant. A consistently forged artifact (content and the artifact's own hash rewritten) is still a miss on both stores, so the version's content_hash is checked independently; no UPDATE or DELETE path exists; artifact then version ordering. Concurrency at 1 microsecond with REFUSE_ON_EVENT_LOOP on: 40 memory and 10 Postgres trials clean, the declared pre-M24 concurrent misses confirmed 50 of 50. Default fetch_url schema_hash identical to HEAD fa64753. Governance audit: one decision added (DECISION-0d384c8d), task order unchanged, re-signing through the CLI. Reviewer mutants 13 of 14, the survivor M12 equivalent. Owner decision: settle these at M23's pre-flight. (1) The orchestrator's criterion executor scope (orchestrator.py about 493) omits ledger_run_id and evidence, so a fetch_url criterion is neither cached nor recorded; the second finding in that spot (M19 round 2); M23's ledger completeness would inherit it. (2) Children inherit the ledger through subagents.py falling back to parent.run_id; correct only while an orchestrator is never itself a child, documented but not asserted. (3) A trailing dot, IDN spelling, or http://h versus http://h/ give different cache keys: a refetch, never a leak. (4) An orphan artifact if recording the version fails after the artifact put. (5) ToolScope accepts an uppercase ledger_run_id that the in-memory store would not match, while RunConfig refuses it. (6) Own-first means a tool widened to PUBLIC_GLOBAL keeps serving its own older PROJECT version until it expires.

knowledge.title: M23 round 1 approved; five caveats to settle at M24's pre-flight
knowledge.text: Approved by Sonnet 5 on source hash fb7c130d, gates recomputed by the reviewer; author mutation run 24 of 24. claim_key has one implementation both stores import, identical across PYTHONHASHSEED 0, 1 and random in separate processes; every AC-73 pair collapses, and NBSP, ideographic space, NEL and ligatures were probed. Concurrency at 1 microsecond on both stores with no-lock mutants detected (29 of 30 duplicates in memory, 150 UniqueViolations on Postgres); three OS processes on one database gave 20 shared claims, 180 contributions, zero forks, each base superseded once, and an xmin check that no contribution landed after its claim's successor. Reviewer used monkeypatches only; no source file mutated. Owner decision: settle these at M24's pre-flight, (1) first. (1) InMemoryLedgerStore.record and PostgresLedgerStore do not check that cited versions are in the claim's tenant and project, nor compute provenance; RunLedger does both, and every model-reachable path goes through it, but LedgerStore, InMemoryLedgerStore and Persistence.ledger_store() are exported, so a caller can store a cross-tenant citation, and migration 0011's comment that the store checks tenancy is false; the fix is the store-layer check, not editing the migration, whose checksum is recorded. (2) Two hashtext collisions crossing in supersede's two-key lock raise a raw DeadlockDetected rather than waiting (20 collisions in 450k keys, the crossing case built deliberately). (3) taken_in appends briefed inputs after the history, so cite-by-URL's reversed scan can rank a briefed older version above the run's own newer fetch, contrary to DECISION-9945a224. (4) NFC then casefold is not canonically closed (Greek iota with dialytika and tonos versus its decomposed capital), spec-literal. (5) record_claim reads the whole ledger back on every call, quadratic in ledger size, not measured; M24's claim-lock sits on it.

knowledge.title: M24 round 1 approved, closing Phase 3 increment 1; C1 to C3 become M24a
knowledge.text: Approved 10:10:42Z by Opus 5 on source hash 0c9970bd, gates recomputed by the reviewer; author mutation run 20 of 20. M23 caveat 1 verified fixed (a store with no evidence store refuses every citation; all ten migration checksums match). Cancellation probed at 16 offsets x 4 trials, contended and not, with pg_locks and pool stats per probe; 60 trials that a cancelled waiter never cancels the holder; the try-lock window held open deterministically; M23's crossing-hashtext deadlock reproduced 30 of 30 against the text-sorted mutant and 0 of 30 on the fix; a killed holder process frees its key; a waiter holds no connection while waiting; example 21 on seven seeds on both stores. Owner decision: complete M24, then a follow-up task M24a before increment 2's specification for C1 to C4. Caveats: (C1) _completed suppresses a re-delivered CancelledError, so on a second cancellation during acquire or during the normal release (claimlock.py, the finally also goes through _completed) the advisory lock is not unlocked and the pooled connection is not returned; the lock is released only when CPython closes the dropped socket; pool slots are lost and after 33 occurrences a checkout raises PoolTimeout after 30 s; reachable only by a double cancel, which no SDK path performs today. (C3, C4) a CancelledError inside a retry attempt, or a waiter's own failure after a successful holder, reopens the 3-attempt budget, so at most 3 attempts is not absolute. (C2) the pipe delimiter in lock keys lets two tenants' keys collide, a wait-timing side channel only, pre-existing from M23. Carried to increment 2: (C5) a waited call that gets a non-2xx records its wait nowhere; (C6) the holder keeps a pooled connection while its operation draws on the same pool; (C7) M24's task requirements omit NFR-25; example 21's editor cites nothing, so its taint check passes vacuously for the corrected claim.

knowledge.title: M24a round 1 approved; budget, wait and encoding caveats carried to increment 2
knowledge.text: Fable 5.1 approved M24a round 1 on source hash 880b57dd (unit 9, regression 1900). C1 verified at unit level and against the live database: repeated cancellation leaves no advisory lock and no pooled connection, where M24 leaked one connection. C2: lock_key injective over 4368 adversarial part lists, 0 collisions. Carried to Phase 3 increment 2 (owner, Complete now, carry all). B1, the first to settle: the budget decrement sits before the backoff sleep, so waiters cancelled during backoff spend the key budget and fail it for everyone with zero operations retried; moving the decrement after the sleep is one line. B2: a success between failures does not restore the budget. W1: _finished waits unboundedly on a thread that never returns, the same property as every to_thread store call. W2: _finished absorbs any BaseException thrown into the task while the future is pending, including KeyboardInterrupt (latent). K1: KeyFailed carries no cause when the key failed through failed_once or a cancelled retry. P1: the M23 transaction-lock names in PostgresLedgerStore._lock still join with a pipe. P2: manifest.py spec_material joins with a pipe before agent_spec_hash, so id a with instructions b|c hashes like id a|b with instructions c, a missed configuration change, predating M24. Also still carried: C5 to C7 and the vacuous taint check in example 21.

knowledge.title: Facts the Phase 3 increment 2 spec review measured in the code, and what the draft changed
knowledge.text: Read-only review 2026-10-11 by an independent Sonnet 5.5 reviewer of the first draft of FR-99 to FR-108. Measured: a node lease is released (orchestrator.py finally after spawn) before _criteria runs, and a released lease refuses calls, so a critic cannot draw on it unless release moves after the gate; _NOT_REPLANNABLE matches by prefix, so critic_failed: budget_exceeded would replan; the node answer is stored after the criteria; contributions carry run_id and node_id only and no ancestry, node_id repeats across replans, and node children cannot spawn (depth 1 hardcoded); RunLedger.supersede builds its contribution from its own run, so a critic contribution needs the store supersede directly with ClaimSuperseded emitted by the orchestrator; the store does not check claim ownership by node or sources against a briefing; EventType is an open str Enum with no DB constraint; manifest columns are added by ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS; no test hardcodes an agent_spec_hash value; P1 old lock name asserted at tests/test_claim_lock.py:489; claimlock _retry decrements before the backoff sleep; _finished cannot tell the future outcome from an exception delivered to the task; KeyFailed never sets __cause__; a waited non-2xx returns at evidence.py obtain with waited in scope; RunLedger.reader is reachable from ToolScope. Fifteen blocking findings, each repaired in the second draft; four owner choices taken on the way (agent_spec_hash prefixed v2, a correction losing a race fails its node and replans, the critic has no tools, the briefing is capped at max_briefing_chars and fails over it).

knowledge.title: M25 round 1 approved; the W2 window becomes M25a before M26
knowledge.text: Opus 5 approved M25 round 1 at 13:57:48Z on source hash 10b16da7, gates recomputed (unit 14, regression 1914, collect-only confirming the 1900 baseline). B1, K1, P1, P2, C5 and example 21 verified; the project.json gate edit (DECISION-11af2ee2) confined to the declared gates; the approved-test edit necessary and not weakening (three _lock mutants killed through it; the pipe join collides). Finding, a regression from M24a: in _finished the guard if future.done() and not future.cancelled(): continue exits the wait loop with interrupted still None when a cancellation is delivered to the caller in the window where the future has just completed, so _completed returns the result and the cancellation is swallowed. Reproduced by passing a future directly (ensure_future of a coroutine adds a loop hop that hides it); a timeout whose deadline coincides with the work settling (same timer instant, or 0.5 ms after) silently fails to fire, and executor.py wait_for around the acquire does not recover: the tool deadline can pass with no signal. Not a leak (0 locks, 0 connections) and AC-77 is met as written, but FR-99 prose (never swallowed) is violated and its sentence the future is done only in the second case is false. Owner decision: complete M25, then M25a before M26 fixes the guard and the same treatment for the non-cancellation branch, corrects FR-99, and kills the dropped mutant, which the reviewer judged not equivalent. Carried: KeyFailed.__init__ sets __cause__ even when None, forcing __suppress_context__ so a KeyFailed raised inside an except hides its context, and unpickling puts the message in .key (cosmetic); W1, C6, B2 and a waited fetch that raises recording no wait stay declared. Also: the plan check run after the manual gate edit cleared the plan approval; re-signed by the owner at 14:16Z after requeueing M25.

knowledge.title: M25a round 1 approved; the W2 window closed
knowledge.text: Sonnet 5 approved M25a round 1 at 15:34:43Z on source hash 6ebfe367, gates recomputed (unit 9, regression 1923). The M25 escalating reviewer reran its three window probes unchanged: M25a honours all 20 trials (cancellation in the settle window, asyncio.timeout_at at and 0.5 ms after the deadline, wait_for right after the acquire and overrunning), M25 d979634 swallows or gives no signal on all 20, M24a honours all 20, so the regression was introduced in M25 and is undone. Reviewer 30-case matrix (five delivery mechanisms x three future outcomes x both orders): 0 mismatches against 18 for M25; 120 randomised repeated-cancellation trials with no swallowed cancellation and no leak. _own compares by identity. Mutants: the cancelled-future own-cancellation mutant is equivalent (both raise CancelledError with no undo); a reviewer mutant counting any exception as own on a cancelled future (M4) survives as a test gap, not a defect, reachable only with a hand-driven coroutine since nothing cancels the work future and asyncio delivers no non-cancellation exception to a task; carried as a note. Governance verified: spec_check 218 to 220 adding exactly FR-109 and AC-82, only the three intended pauses. Still carried: KeyFailed forced __suppress_context__ and pickling (cosmetic), W1, C6, B2 and a waited fetch that raises recording no wait (declared, FR-99).

knowledge.title: M26 round 1 approved; four caveats become M26a before M27
knowledge.text: Fable 5.1 approved M26 round 1 at 09:11:22Z on source hash f17a7f2e, gates recomputed (unit 58, regression 1981); the review stalled in item 8 and was resumed, items 1 to 7 complete before the stall. Verified: a 20000-view fuzz of the five signals against an independent FR-102 oracle; the node-subject rule identical on both stores across a child orchestrator, a replanned run, a sibling top-level run and an explicit ledger_run_id; bypass controls land when the store check is removed; NFR-29 against git archive c35a319 with event streams, requests and row multisets identical; a cancelled run still writes its gate row; a store failure fails the node loudly with the lease released and no GateEvaluated; AC-44 tracking caught a real stray SYN-m12 run on its first outing. Caveats, settled in M26a by owner decision: (1) FR-103 and AC-78 say record_validation is reachable from no ToolScope, but every tool scope carries _runner (api.py tool scope construction), so a custom tool can certify its own claim; a model cannot, since it only supplies arguments; the reachability test checks field names only and would keep passing; _runner is load-bearing at eight orchestrator sites. (2) 0012 comment says the foreign keys back the store check, but only node-subject tenancy is backed; claim-subject tenancy and ledger membership rest on the store transactional check (a recurrence of M23 caveat 1: a migration comment asserting what the schema does not enforce). (3) README: with no critic configured, a tool_succeeds criterion after a critic criterion now runs its side effects before criterion_not_available. (4) a claim whose only contributions are the critic own never fires low_confidence, live once M27 runs the critic. Process: the reviewer passed the raw DATABASE_URL to apply_migrations and a ProgrammingError echoed it; self-disclosed and fixed; the recorded rotation triggers (reachable from other machines, reused, shared use) do not apply. Carried unchanged: W1, C6, B2, a waited fetch that raises recording no wait, KeyFailed context and pickling, M25a M4 branch.

knowledge.title: M26a round 1 approved; six follow-ups and the suite time go to M27 pre-flight
knowledge.text: Opus 5 approved M26a round 1 at 12:26:41Z on source hash 22f32a7f, gates recomputed (unit 8, regression 1989). 0013 verified on throwaway schemas with the store out of the loop: through 0012 cross-ledger, cross-tenant and cross-project claim subjects land; through 0013 each is refused by verifications_claim_in_ledger while a same-ledger claim and a node subject land; claims.claim_id being the primary key makes the composite foreign key airtight; all 12 checksums match. Follow-ups for M27 pre-flight (owner): (1) Runner.record_validation docstring still says no tool reaches the Runner, the withdrawn guarantee; (2) rename the approved M26 test test_record_validation_is_reachable_from_no_tool, whose name asserts what M26a withdrew; (3) AC-83 says every shipped tool runs with record_validation watched when four of nine do, the static check over agentsdk being the stronger proof; (4) the approved M26 signal oracle still encodes the pre-amendment low_confidence rule and passes only because its generator never builds a critic-only claim; (5) 0013 cannot apply on a database where M26 already recorded a cross-ledger claim subject (ADD CONSTRAINT validates existing rows; the DO block rolls back cleanly), stated in README and SPEC since 0013 cannot be edited once applied; (6) the walk docstring claims more than depth 1: a writer wrapped one level deeper escapes, and ledger._store.__self__ is the Runner, the declared reach. Owner also asked for the suite time (8m06s against the 9m50s gate limit) to be profiled at M27 pre-flight before anything changes.

knowledge.title: M27 round 1 approved; the critic label clauses and four caveats go to M28 pre-flight
knowledge.text: Sonnet 5 approved M27 round 1 at 13:57:20Z on source hash a23d4e3b, gates recomputed detached at the 25-minute limit (unit 21, regression 2010). Verified: exactly once per execution across a replan carrying a node forward, two nodes racing on one claim (second refused already superseded, rerun gated afresh), cancellation during the critic (ran once, no rows) and a store failure after the critic (in memory only: Postgres returns a fresh store object per call, so that monkeypatch never applied); event order GateEvaluated, ClaimSuperseded, CriticVerdict, PlanNodeFinished on both stores; example 22 live passed with a real output_contract_violation replanned. Finding: four NFR-28 mutants survive all tests, including dropping taking_in at the corrected answer (orchestrator.py, the corrected return); AC-79 requires the corrected answer at least as tainted as the critic inputs and the orchestrator labels carrying the critic provenance, correct in the code but undemonstrated, because every taint check compares against the page and the critic shares the page taint (third recurrence after M24 example 21 and M26 gate-row provenance). Caveats: a whitespace-only or NUL reason passes the verdict schema minLength then fails NewContribution outside the try, leaving a critic run with no critic row or CriticVerdict and the node node_error; paraphrases on a node with no claims are free strings; corrections [] with corrected swaps the answer superseding nothing; approved keeps the child label (per spec). Owner decisions: settle at M28 pre-flight, no M27a: a test tainting the critic result alone; whitespace and NUL refused at the schema boundary; paraphrases constrained to the node claims; an answer-only correction (corrected with no corrections) is valid; the Postgres store-failure-after-critic case.

knowledge.title: M28 round 1 approved, closing Phase 3 increment 2; four items carried to the next phase pre-flight
knowledge.text: Fable 5.1 approved M28 round 1 at 17:46:13Z on source hash 46d03d73, gates recomputed detached (unit 16, regression 2034). Verified: the M27 label mutants now killed by a critic result tainted alone with SECRET_BEARING; _RECORDABLE checked against the ledger _text over every code point in four positions with re.search, 0 mismatches, no over-refusal; the calibration arithmetic recomputed by hand, 300 random row orders and all 24 tie interleavings unchanged; the exit signal on 23 further seeds with three controls, one raising DOUBTFUL to 0.9 to show the expected set is not read back. Reviewer correction: dropping labels.append(critic.provenance) survives the new label test but is killed by the existing test_the_orchestrator_hears_the_critic test, so the clause is pinned. Disclosed: in memory the two supersede calls do not overlap on threads, on Postgres they do; example 23 taint checks are structurally right but vacuous in its corpus, since the critic provenance equals the pages, and the unit test is what pins it. Carried to the next phase pre-flight (owner): (1) corrected_answer is not guarded, so a lone surrogate fails the node output_not_stored after the verdict is recorded and a NUL is stored in the artifact; guard stored text at one boundary, not field by field, the same defect class as the M27 caveat one field over; (2) no_claims can never appear in a per-signal fired column, since the unit is a claim; (3) a critic row whose gate row predates since still counts in the critic table; (4) NFR-29 requests-and-events clause is argued, not tested; and example 23 taint checks stay vacuous until a corpus taints the critic differently from the pages.

knowledge.title: Before the Phase 4 spec: how the OpenAI Agents SDK pauses and resumes a run (RunState, openai-agents 0.23.1)
knowledge.text: Read from the openai-agents 0.23.1 wheel source (agents/run_state.py, 5472 lines; run_context.py; _run_state_agent_identity.py; run_internal/turn_resolution.py) and the official human-in-the-loop docs, 2026-10-13. (1) Only tool approval interrupts: a tool declares needs_approval, a bool or a callable of context, arguments and call id; the run then returns, not raises, with result.interruptions, and result.to_state() gives a RunState. Approval is run-wide: an interruption inside a nested agent-as-tool surfaces on the outer run. (2) The snapshot is the whole in-memory run as one JSON document: turn, current agent reference, original and pending input, every model response, generated and session items, usage, approval records, tool invocations, the application context with metadata, guardrail results, current step, last processed response, trace, sandbox state and any pending session write. It carries $schemaVersion, now 1.18 after 18 bumps; older released versions stay readable and newer ones are refused fail-fast. (3) No code is serialized: agents and tools are found again by name from the root agent passed to from_json, walked breadth first, with duplicate names given stable identities; the application configuration must be unchanged between pause and resume, and MCP calls need recipient bindings. (4) On resume the model is not called again: the interrupted turn is resolved from the recorded last processed response, approved calls execute, a rejected call returns a rejection message to the model, then the loop continues. (5) Decisions are per call id, with sticky always_approve and always_reject scoped to one agent and an optional rejection message, all stored in the snapshot. (6) Trust boundary: from_json and from_string do not authenticate the snapshot or who approved; the docs now say keep snapshots server-side and apply only authorized, single-use decisions (openai-agents-python PR 5105, Sep 2026). Related bugs: interruptions returned mutable aliases of the pending approvals (PR 4409), and approval was not honoured on resume when a context was passed (issue 4244). Independently restored copies must not be resumed concurrently against one session. (7) For this SDK: the store is already the record (NFR-3: runs, messages, events, manifests, plan states), and outcomes.py already defines RunInterruption with a resume_token, InterruptionKind (tool_approval and four others) and ApprovalRequired, while executor step 4 auto-allows (ADR-29: in process in Phase 4, durable in Phase 6). The design questions for P4: a store-derived pause, with a paused run row and a pending interruption row, versus a versioned snapshot blob; resume executing the recorded call without a new model call; decisions as server-side rows bound to tenant, project and principal, single-use; at most one resume at a time (an advisory lock, as the claim-lock); refusing resume when the agent spec hash or tool set changed since the pause; whether the node lease and budget stay held while waiting; expiry; and how an interruption inside an orchestrated child surfaces on the parent run.

knowledge.title: Facts the Phase 4 increment 1 spec review measured in the code, and what the second draft changed
knowledge.text: Read-only review of the first draft by Sonnet 5, 2026-10-13, claims checked first-hand by the orchestrator. Measured: batches of one turn run strictly one after another (loop.py _execute_tool_calls) and _results asserts only Completed and Failed are reachable, as tests/test_primitives.py asserts; executor step 4 is an empty stub and before_tool handles only REJECT and MODIFY, so REQUIRE_APPROVAL and HALT are ignored today; ToolSpec.approval_policy is never read and not in schema_hash; ApprovalRequired and RunInterruption exist unused; RunHandle.cancel crosses threads with call_soon_threadsafe while store writes must run on a worker thread (FR-81), so decide is a coroutine; tool functions receive only their arguments and an optional scope, so an approved hash needs a typed channel; the M10 file tools bind only CreateFileW, GetFinalPathNameByHandleW, GetFileInformationByHandleEx, ReadFile and CloseHandle, and open without delete sharing; runs has only a primary key, so a composite key to it needs an ALTER in 0014; a child holds its max_concurrent_subagents slot for its whole run and its RunConfig carries no approval settings; the orchestrator spawns at depth 1 and critic runs have no tools; GateEvaluated is the precedent for a node event on the orchestrator stream. The first draft blocked on eight points: waiting inside prepare would serialise approvals and contradict P4-D6; decide could not be thread-safe as cancel is; no channel for the approved hash; NFR-33 falsely said no new Win32 calls; the composite keys needed an ALTER and sticky semantics were untestable; stored-text checks and fault injection were missing; the crash rule contradicted P4-D2; and orchestration plumbing was unspecified. The owner then decided P4-D13 to P4-D15 (DECISION-af27465a) and the second draft settled every finding.

knowledge.title: M29 round 1 approved; two schema and listing findings go to M30 pre-flight
knowledge.text: Opus 5 approved M29 round 1 at 12:47:43Z on source hash 9b084719, gates recomputed detached (unit 24, regression 2060). Verified: _STORABLE agrees with unstorable_reason on 4001 strings and an approved verdict with an empty or blank corrected_answer still passes; the NFR-29 fixture has 266 leaves, 13 dropped (timing and cost), 3 ids substituted, 246 of 253 compared literally, and killed three of four mutants including a one-word tool description change; tenancy held in 100 checks on both stores through the API and raw SQL; 0014 applies over M28-shaped rows and is idempotent; 16 illegal row shapes refused and all 6 legal ones accepted; the new tables held 0 rows after the suite. Findings, confirmed by the orchestrator in the code, owner chose to settle them at M30 pre-flight: (1) interruption_decisions.standing_id references standing_decisions by a single column while every other 0014 reference is tenant-composite, so the schema alone lets a decision name another tenant standing decision, the defect 0013 fixed for claims one migration earlier; the Python guard that closes it in both stores is untested (two mutants survived); fix by migration 0015 adding UNIQUE (standing_id, tenant_id, project_id) and a composite key, and a test of the guard. (2) InMemoryInterruptionStore.interruptions treats a run_id canonical_id cannot read as no filter and returns the whole tenant, while interruption() one method below treats it as not found and PostgreSQL returns nothing; fix to return nothing. Lower priority: the non tool_approval refusal is untested in memory; the fixture exclusion by field name is wider than needed; the critic join would match rows lacking critic_run on None; AC-85 no-update pin is a name regex; standing seq values differ between stores, only order is specified; the fixture pins requests and events, not stored rows.

knowledge.title: M30 round 1 approved; four approval caveats go to M31 pre-flight, two of them fail-open
knowledge.text: Fable 5.1 approved M30 round 1 at 17:19:58Z on source hash 7634279a, gates recomputed detached (unit 49, regression 2109). Verified: NFR-30 under a fault-injecting store proxy on both stores (append_interruption, interruption reads, standing reads, append_decision for expiry and decide all failing), cancellation at nine awaits including inside an async describe and predicate, 24 decision-versus-expiry races at the expiry instant, mixed concurrency_safe batches, with a bypass mutant control showing the probe detects a call run unapproved; AC-32 edit honest (972 of 1944 golden specs declare REQUIRE_APPROVAL, the AUTO replace is the identity for every other, golden literals unchanged); NFR-32 by diffing a 7-call scripted run against 62cc198 (724 leaves, 14 differ, all wall-clock); 0015 applied and idempotent, single-column standing reference gone; example 24 live passed. Caveats, the first two confirmed by the orchestrator in executor.py and escalated, owner chose to settle all four at M31 pre-flight before the write tools: (1) the request records dict(call.arguments), a shallow copy, while step 6 executes the live tool_call.arguments, so a hook holding its replacement can change what runs after the approver saw it, for up to approval_timeout; execute from a deep copy of exactly what was approved; (2) needs_approval is honoured only when it returns the True singleton, so 1 or yes runs unasked, failing open; refuse a non-bool with ToolApprovalCheckFailed; (3) ApprovalRequested can be missing when an approver polling the store decides between recording and the run first read (3 of 5 rounds in memory, 0 of 5 on PostgreSQL); emit right after recording; (4) decide(sticky=True) raises when the standing write fails although the decision is recorded, and sends no wake, so the run adopts it only on the five-second re-read. Theme: the gate trusted tool-author code to be well-formed and failed open when it was not.

knowledge.title: M31 round 1 approved; a model-reachable pool stall and three follow-ups go to M32 pre-flight
knowledge.text: Sonnet 5 approved M31 round 1 at 04:36:42Z on source hash 9c531471, gates recomputed (unit 39, regression 2148). Process incident, disclosed by the reviewer and verified by the orchestrator: two of its mutation runs overlapped, breaking the one-session rule, left agentsdk/executor.py with a mutant line and leaked an example 25 run into example-tenant; it reversed all three, and every file is byte-identical to the baseline apart from CLI-written .genesis records, no if False remains in agentsdk, the live contentHash equals the gate source_hash, example-tenant runs 19 to 19, total runs 10351 to 10351, the interruption tables at 0 rows and no orphan temporary files. Verified: about 90 confinement paths (dot-dot spellings, extended and device prefixes, UNC, device names, streams, 8.3 aliases, trailing dots, junctions, symlinks, dangling links and hard links at the target and in the path) with the outside tree unchanged and no refusal naming an outside path; a junction swapped after describe, and one swapped just after the pre-open check, both refused, with controls showing a naive writer and a copy without the final-path check escaping; mutating the model arguments, ToolCall.arguments and a listed request never changed what was written, and a model-sent or hook-injected approved was refused or overridden. Correction by the orchestrator to one reviewer caveat: removing the _open_inside final-path check survives the M31 gate file but is killed by the M10 test of a link swapped between check and open, which runs in the regression gate. Follow-ups, owner chose M32 pre-flight: (1) model-reachable: edit_file counts overlapping occurrences by testing every position, quadratic, with no cap on old; a 1 MB file and a 500000-character old took 14.84 s on a pool thread, during describe, before anyone is asked, and the pool has four threads; cap the length of old. (2) Any name matching the temporary-file shape is withheld from list, glob and grep, so a model can hide a file there, and a crash leaves temporary files nothing sweeps; withhold only names this process created, and sweep orphans. (3) The README limitation understates the refusal: any open reader, even one sharing delete, blocked the replace in 43 of 60 writes; say so. (4) The M30 sticky early wake is unpinned: removing it leaves the tests passing at 40 s rather than 5 s because the five-second re-read masks it; pin it with a timing bound. Also weak: the non-bool predicate mutant was killed by a hang, not an assertion. Example 25 live was not probed by the reviewer (covered offline on both stores).

knowledge.title: M32 round 1 approved, but three exit-signal bullets were vacuous; repaired in round 2 before increment 1 closes
knowledge.text: Opus 5 approved M32 round 1 (control f18a9465) on source hash fa7fc52d, gates recomputed (unit 17, regression 2165). No reachable behavioural defect: its own orchestrated probe saw five approved calls replaced at MoveFileExW in issue order, a rejected one never ran, decisions fired exactly at expires_at across eight repetitions matched disk, cancellation at two depths decided every pending interruption cancel on both stores with _live empty, and the M31 pool stall is closed (0.016 s against 14.84 s). Findings, confirmed by the orchestrator from source: C1 the contention bullet of scripts/26 reads not race or ..., so it passes with no contention (the reviewer replaced the race with a sleep and every check passed); C2 base.txt two edits commute, so files == expected pins no order; C3 the ran-once clause compares call keys with their own set, so it sees duplicate ids, not duplicate executions (an executor running every approved call twice passed the signal); C6 v.decision is dereferenced unguarded, so a view with no decision, the NFR-30 failure itself, raises AttributeError instead of a FAIL; C4 removing the top-level emit hangs the test on handle.events() rather than failing it; C5 task_id on the child own stream is unpinned; C7 the critic test is a tautology that never runs a critic (pinned elsewhere at tests/test_critic.py); C8 the sweep prefix test can match a sibling target whose name extends this one. Fourth recurrence of a check written against something it shares with the thing it checks (M24 example 21, M26 gate-row provenance, M27 taint, M32 exit signal): make it a standing review question. Process: the reviewer killed a gate at 150 s, leaving 49 SYN-m32 runs, and removed them by id; verified by the orchestrator: interruption tables 0/0/0, runs 10351, example-tenant 19, no SYN-m32 rows, no advisory locks, no mutant markers. Second round running with a one-session-rule slip. While recording, genesis control requeue --help requeued the task: that CLI takes --help as an argument, never pass it.

knowledge.title: M32 round 2 rejected: the rejection bullet of the exit signal had no witness; every check needs one
knowledge.text: Fable 5.1 rejected M32 round 2 at 10:13:09Z on source hash d5dc57af. C1 to C8 hold: 16 runtime mutants on memory and 5 on Postgres each failed on the named label, C4 fails in about 15 to 31 s on the until bound, C7 in 1.6 s, the sweep reaches no other target orphan across ten name shapes, and the session guard stops a second session before any store read and is released within 0.05 s after taskkill, pytest.exit and CTRL_BREAK; AC-65 nested session still passes. F1, confirmed by the orchestrator from source: every rejection reason reached its writer is all() over principal rejections, true when there are none, and the approval screen swallowed the InterruptionExpired of a late reject, so a screen late for b.txt reported a clean sweep on both stores without any SDK mutation. The orchestrator found the same hole in the issue-order bullet: true with no executions, and with no writer having two. Lesson, fifth recurrence (M24 example 21, M26, M27, M32 C1, M32 F1): every bullet of a signal needs a witness that what it checks happened, and all() over a filtered list is the shape to look for. Example 23 offline is witnessed (len(lost) == 1, expected critic runs) but its live lost-race and judged-once bullets pass when no race occurs; owner chose to record it and fix at the next phase pre-flight by reporting such live bullets as not exercised. Carried as declared: counted defines undecided as membership in the pending listing; duplicate decisions are pinned only through the race label; AGENTSDK_TEST_SESSION admits any session that sets it, by design a guard against accidents only. The reviewer mutated no repository file: every mutant was a runtime monkeypatch; the store is at baseline (10351 runs, 19 example-tenant, interruption tables 0). Harness note: project.json keeps round 1 independent-review evidence as pass while KICKOFF computes stale.

knowledge.title: M32 round 3 approved, closing Phase 4 increment 1; three exit-signal caveats go to increment 2 pre-flight
knowledge.text: Sonnet 5 approved M32 round 3 at 14:07:30Z on source hash 76f708c4 (unit 24, regression 2172), the cheapest of fourteen rounds at about 120k tokens and 18 minutes; it touched no source file, and its first cleanup hit a foreign-key error and was rerun, verified by the orchestrator to leave the store at baseline (10351 runs, 19 example-tenant, interruption tables 0, no locks). Caveats, owner chose increment 2 pre-flight, reproduced by the orchestrator relay: (1) checks 1 to 7 run live and 8 to 11 offline only, so a single skipped approval, or a, d and base together, passes the live run and is caught only offline; a files check is impossible live because a real model writes freely. (2) The rejection witness, a principal rejection with a reason, is met without b.txt if the race losing reject carries a message: it passed on 3 of 6 seeds with b.txt never decided; today decide_twice passes no message, so the protection is an accident of one omitted keyword; the shared bullet should name b.txt itself, as the offline sources bullet does. (3) re.IGNORECASE folds Unicode beyond NTFS (the Kelvin sign), cosmetic: it deletes only stale garbage. Also at the same pre-flight: example 23 live lost-race and judged-once bullets (DECISION-e75ad00a). Correction to the relay: control bac66b5a is not corrupted; its bytes are e2 80 94, a real em dash, at HEAD and now; the mojibake was a cp1252 console decoding UTF-8. Lesson, sixth recurrence: a witness must name its subject, not a property its subject happens to have.

knowledge.title: Before the Phase 4 increment 2 spec: MCP 2026-07-28, the mcp 2.3.0 client, comparator SDKs and client-side attacks
knowledge.text: Researched 2026-10-15, primary sources; the two load-bearing facts verified by the orchestrator. Spec: the current revision is 2026-07-28 (modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog), stateless: the initialize handshake and Mcp-Session-Id are removed, each request carries protocol version and client capabilities in _meta, servers MUST implement server/discover, list_changed and resource updates come only on an opted-in subscriptions/listen stream, SSE resumability is removed (a broken stream is re-issued as a new request), Multi Round-Trip Requests replace server-initiated requests (a result with resultType input_required carries inputRequests; the client retries with inputResponses), list results carry ttlMs and cacheScope, tasks moved to an extension. 2025-11-25 and earlier are legacy; a dual-era client SHOULD probe server/discover and fall back to initialize, not keyed to one error code. Deprecated in 2026-07-28: roots, sampling, logging, dynamic client registration (replaced by Client ID Metadata Documents); HTTP+SSE deprecated since 2025-03-26. Transports: stdio and Streamable HTTP; on stdio cancel is notifications/cancelled, shutdown is close stdin then terminate (Job Objects on Windows). Tools: paginated, inputSchema JSON Schema 2020-12, optional outputSchema with structuredContent the client SHOULD validate, annotations MUST be treated as untrusted unless the server is trusted, isError results go to the model, a human SHOULD be able to deny calls, aggregating clients SHOULD prefix names and not rely on serverInfo.name; names 1 to 128 of A-Za-z0-9_.-. Elicitation is optional, form or url mode, secrets only by url mode, which the client must show in full and open only with consent. Authorization: optional, HTTP only (stdio takes credentials from the environment); OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, RFC 9728 protected resource metadata, RFC 8707 resource on every authorization and token request, audience-bound tokens, no token passthrough, credentials keyed by issuer, step-up on insufficient_scope; never open an authorization URL through a shell (CVE-2025-6514 in mcp-remote was RCE that way). Client library: mcp 2.3.0 (2026-10-02, PyPI verified, requires httpx2); 2.x has a single Client with mode auto (probe then fall back), legacy or a pinned version; list cache with cache_mode; timeouts raise MCPError -32001; cancelling the awaiting task sends notifications/cancelled; on 2026-07-28 connections sampling, elicitation and roots callbacks raise NoBackChannelError, and whether 2.x handles input_required client-side is unverified; OAuthClientProvider over httpx2; on Windows stdio servers run in a Job Object with kill-on-close and stop by hard kill after stdin closes. Comparators: OpenAI Agents SDK has MCPServerStdio and MCPServerStreamableHttp (SSE deprecated), cache_tools_list, tool_filter allow then block, optional server prefix, require_approval always, never, per tool or a callable that does not see the arguments, no result trust labels; Claude Agent SDK names tools mcp__server__tool, blocks them until allowed, runs no OAuth itself (the app supplies tokens), refreshes the list on list_changed, warns of prompt injection; Google ADK and Pydantic AI have toolsets with filters and prefixes. The official MCP Registry is a preview holding metadata only; no standard exists for credential brokering beyond url-mode elicitation and enterprise-managed authorization; vendor gateways hold per-user tokens. Attacks to design against: tool poisoning, rug pulls (a tool changing after approval), cross-server shadowing, prompt injection through results, token theft and passthrough, SSRF in OAuth discovery, malicious stdio launch commands.

knowledge.title: Facts the Phase 4 increment 2 spec review measured in the code, and what the second draft changes
knowledge.text: Read-only review of the first draft, 2026-10-18, claims verified by the orchestrator where marked. Verified: migration 0014 checks kind = tool_approval and trigger in policy, predicate, hook, and decisions are approve or reject with principal iff source principal and expiry or cancel only reject, so input requests need new constraints, not a wider kind; without a ContextPolicy every run is sent the Runner-wide registry (api.py:987), shared by every tenant, so MCP descriptions would reach every agent; the executor wraps a whole tool call in asyncio.wait_for(timeout_seconds) (executor.py:565), so a call waiting for input dies at its timeout; tests/test_distribution.py:236-237, requirements.txt, pyproject examples and scripts/requirements.txt pin mcp==2.2.0; pyproject packages list agentsdk and agentsdk.providers only; the draft cited FR-36 for validation (it is FR-5 step 2), FR-40 for the cap (FR-41) and FR-42 for error provenance (FR-40). Reported, for the second draft: one migration cannot serve three milestones; the tool registry raises on duplicates at registration and has no removal, and a per-run tenant-filtered view refreshed each turn is new work, since the view is built once at run start; provenance comes from ToolOutput.source_uri or the schema hash; standing decisions match on agent and tool name and only for trigger policy (loop.py:710-718); after_tool hooks can replace provenance (a recorded risk); RunEvent needs a run, so connection-level events must be emitted on the run that caused them; briefed inputs are artifacts, so a resource read is stored as an artifact first; Message has no provenance field; a server schema is validated on the loop thread, so a hostile pattern is a stall risk; a url-mode URL may carry a token; Runner has no aclose today and examples never close one. Unverified: whether httpx2 installs beside httpx 0.28.1.

knowledge.title: M33 round 1 rejected: starting and listing an MCP server had no bound, the seventh bounded-one-path defect
knowledge.text: Opus 5 rejected M33 round 1 at 09:41:56Z on source hash 2058f874 (unit 40, regression 2212); it touched no source file, its probes used in-memory persistence, the store is at baseline, and the reject did not change the content hash (.genesis is excluded). Defect, reproduced by the orchestrator relay and confirmed by the orchestrator in code: _Connection._open awaits the server start, the discover or initialize exchange and the listing with no timeout (only call_tool passes read_timeout_seconds), so a server that starts but never speaks MCP hangs the run: a launcher printing one non-JSON banner line then sleeping, and a server that reads but never answers, both hung past 25 s with no result, while a missing command and an immediate exit fail fast; and the listing loop bounds tools, not pages, so empty pages with a cursor loop forever. prepare() runs at api.py before the manifest, so the run hangs before it is recorded. This violates FR-124 and AC-90, undeclared, reachable by ordinary misconfiguration. Pattern: the path under attention was bounded and its sibling left unbounded, the seventh appearance; the repair sweeps every wait on server-controlled input. Caveat promoted: a profile entry srv__* allowed a tool named exactly srv, because partition yields no separator. Accepted with notes: the output-error mapping keys on the library message, pinned by mcp==2.3.0 and the output-mismatch test; the inherited environment is the library twelve names, missing TMP, undeclared. Not completed by the reviewer and accepted: a pathological-pattern schema (blocked interpreter shutdown, already a declared risk), example 27 live.

knowledge.title: M33 round 2 rejected: a request write to a server that stopped reading had no bound, and aclose did not stop reopening
knowledge.text: Fable 5.1 rejected M33 round 2 at 06:52:05Z on source hash 960ad6a3 (unit 47, regression 2219); no source file touched, the store at baseline. Defect 1, reproduced by the orchestrator relay and confirmed in the mcp library source: the dispatcher writes a request first (jsonrpc_dispatcher.py line 410, a bare zero-buffer send) and arms the read clock only after it (line 414), so read_timeout_seconds cannot bound the write; a server that stops reading its input wedges the run once a request fills the pipe: freeze then a 70 KB or 2 MB call then any further call hung past 40 s, while the round 2 test shape (one call after the wedge) passed and a 30 KB control stayed bounded. The round 2 brief claimed the call path was already bounded; it was not, and the gap was in the round own deliverable. Defect 2, confirmed in code: McpClients.aclose pops this loop connections but records no closed state, and connection() recreates any missing one, so a run in flight starts a new server on a closed Runner, against NFR-39. The family recurring inside its own repair: enumerating awaits has missed once per round; state the invariant (the SDK owns the deadline of every await that can block on a peer) and test it structurally (a second call after a wedged write must return). The reviewer also located a suspect for the one-off 68 percent gate stall near test 1508 in test_phase2_readiness.py, not reproduced, and noted faulthandler_timeout dumps C thread stacks only, so an asyncio stall would show the loop polling, not the stuck coroutine. The connect overshoot of about 2 s past connect_timeout is the library PROCESS_TERMINATION_TIMEOUT after stdin closes. Its suite run had 3 live-gateway failures from its own quoted BASE_URL export, green on rerun.

knowledge.title: M33 round 3 rejected: a connection held across aclose started a server no later aclose could reach
knowledge.text: Sonnet 5 rejected M33 round 3 at 08:06:26Z on source hash eb33cbc8 (unit 50, regression 2222, both verified real from the evidence files by the orchestrator relay). Defect, reproduced: close() never marked a connection final, and ensure() gated only on a live client or a spent restart, so a _Connection retained past aclose -- by a tool from an earlier turn -- started a fresh server; aclose had popped it, so no later aclose could reach it (NFR-39). connection() did refuse a closed loop, which covered the next turn refresh, the path round 3 tested, and missed the retained-object path: the third round running of a guarded path beside an unguarded one.
