Secondary, kept: serve() unset the client whatever session was current, so a call restarting the server during a discard left a live but unusable server with the restart spent. Measured: a 0.7 s loop stall kept the 1 s wedge margin, 1.6 s lost it and misreported an honest timeout. Rounds 1 and 2 repairs re-probed by the relay and holding. Process note: the reviewer stopped at the first defect and took the gate evidence on trust; the relay verified the evidence. Root cause of three rejections, by the orchestrator: lifecycle state spread over several flags checked differently by different paths; the repair is structural -- one gate for every start, made final under one lock -- tested for every holder, not the path a reviewer used.

knowledge.title: M33 round 4 rejected: a server schema with no regular expression still validated in process, unbounded
knowledge.text: Opus 5 rejected M33 round 4 at 12:20:07Z on source hash 56539250 (unit 71, regression 2243; the reviewer re-ran the gates after a genesis gate --check accident overwrote the evidence, same hash and counts). Defect, reproduced by the orchestrator relay and confirmed by the orchestrator: round 4 isolated only schemas carrying pattern or patternProperties, on the premise that any other could not stall; a 1.4 KB schema of $ref-chained anyOf with no regular expression took 118 s at depth 20, about 4x per level, in process: at input (executor step 2, to_thread with no deadline, and MCP tools carry no timeout_seconds) and at output (the library validator on the engine loop, so the call deadline on that loop could not fire, and aclose did not return within 45 s with the server alive, NFR-39). Also measured by the orchestrator: check_schema of a duplicating nested schema is exponential too. knowledge.title: M33 round 5 rejected: the alias wildcard allowed a registered tool under a configured alias, a finding round 4 had named and round 5 dropped
knowledge.text: Fable 5.1 rejected M33 round 5 at 15:44:25Z on source hash 71672b3e (unit 81, regression 2253, both re-run by the reviewer). _McpAllowlist.check allowed a name when the text before its first double underscore was a configured alias whose wildcard the profile held, and never asked whether the name was a tool of that server, so a registered first-party host__wipe ran for a profile of host__* once a server aliased host was configured (reproduced first-hand: ALLOW with the server, DENY without it, DENY with only other). Round 4 had named this as its third finding; the round 5 brief did not mention it, as fix, deferral or dispute, so the reviewer re-found it. Process lesson: the previous reject reason is the next round contract; every repair brief carries a ledger of every finding and caveat of every earlier rejection with its status, and a missing or false row is itself a finding. Everything round 5 was built for held under attack: isolation failed closed on 11 malformed child outputs, kills and timeouts; remote refs by http, file, UNC and a base-URI trick were unreadable with no connection; deep anyOf ended at 10.09 s; the caller deadline fired as _Closed; NFR-39 held. Caveats carried into round 6: a NUL in one listed schema made the whole server unavailable; the one-batch 10 s listing check refused honest listings past about 45k properties; the checker child stdin is written before its clock (not server-reachable); the static bounds test missed async for, .get, .recv, os.read, readline, run_until_complete, check_output and helpers in other modules; secret.json (18 bytes, untracked, not ignored) sits at the root and is in the content hash.

knowledge.title: A genesis record written while a gate runs is lost when the gate writes project.json back
knowledge.text: On 2026-10-19 DECISION-e8746c66 was recorded at about 18:20Z while the M33 gate (started 18:10Z) was running; the gate wrote .genesis/project.json back when it ended and the decision vanished, though the CLI had printed Recorded. tasks.outcome: Postgres schema and stores persist runs, messages, run_events and exactly one execution manifest per run, every row tenant-scoped and the trace reconstructable in order

evidence.human: Independent L4 Delta Reviewer (fresh session, owner account)
evidence.reason: Delta APPROVED. Verified exactly 6 files (+204/-17) changed since f2ab64b, nothing else outside .genesis/ bookkeeping; full suite 407 passed. All four changes individually mutation-tested with restores verified by SHA-256 (git status clean, orphan count unchanged at 979). (1) max_turns=True: deleted the column_rejection_reason bool guard alone -> 2 genuine FAILURES (not errors), 405 passed; restored, deleted the RunConfig bool guard alone -> 2 genuine FAILURES, 405 passed; restored. Both guards are independently pinned; JSONB still accepts a bool (column_rejection_reason(True,'JSONB') is None), so the refusal is INTEGER-specific, not a blanket ban. (2) Schema tests: confirmed pg_get_constraintdef/information_schema assertions run in a throwaway namespace that is dropped in a finally (verified 0 leftover m5_probe_ schemas after my runs); confirmed not brittle to reformatting (Postgres normalises the constraint text server-side, independent of schema.sql whitespace/comments/constraint naming). Independently mutated runs.max_turns INTEGER->BIGINT: new test dies (AssertionError: bigint != integer); swapped in the exact f2ab64b test file against the same mutated schema.sql and confirmed it passes (1 passed) -- the old test genuinely could not see this class of defect, the new one can. (3) _safe_finish: traced control flow in api.py -- the success-path finish_run call at line 328 has no enclosing try, so its exception propagates to Runner.run's outer except, which calls the swallowing _safe_finish a second time (itself wrapped in try/except pass) and returns FAILED with the real finish_run error as result.error; this matches both new tests exactly. The SimpleNamespace fake used for runner._persistence exposes exactly the RunRecorder/session_store_for/event_sink_for surface Runner.run actually calls (verified against Persistence's real attributes in persistence.py) -- a faithful duck-typed fake of the seam under test, not a fake proving only itself. The asymmetry (error path swallows, success path surfaces) is the right call: a completed run whose finish_run fails must not be reported as cleanly completed when its terminal state was never durably recorded. (4) _serialisation_reason extraction: read unstorable_reason/_named_unstorable_reason/_serialisation_reason together -- the extraction is a pure lift of the existing try/except body into a named function with an unchanged call chain, so unstorable_reason answers identically before and after and the named layer still wins (checked first). Mutation-verified both halves are now independently pinned: gutting the named layer's non-finite branch -> 1 genuine failure (the new diagnosis-string test), 406 passed; restored; neutering _serialisation_reason to always return None -> 12 genuine failures including the new backstop-specific test, 395 passed; restored. This closes the exact gap the round-9 approval flagged as caveat (3) (KNOWLEDGE-fd4720a4). Regression: all 5 test files (M1-M4 coverage in test_model_client/test_tool_executor/test_agent_loop/test_primitives, M5 in test_persistence) pass together at 407; no source outside the 6 files touched. JSONB float>=1e16 normalising to int on read: correctly recorded as a limitation rather than fixed -- it is Postgres's own jsonb numeric representation, precision-losing only above 1e16, no run fails, and there is no in-scope fix short of a bigger architectural change (e.g. NUMERIC storage) that this narrow delta should not attempt. Database left undamaged: orphan count still exactly 979 after all mutation runs; 0 leftover throwaway schemas. No new defects found in the four changes.

limitations: Carried from M4 review: a tool on the FINAL turn executes with no turn left to consume its result, so a side-effecting tool can fire on a turn whose outcome is max_turns_exceeded. Matches LLD 3.10 literally and is harmless for Phase 0's echo tool, but must be revisited in Phase 2 when tools do more than echo.

Carried from M4 review: RunResult.usage is zeroed when Runner's total boundary catches a non-SDK exception, even though the ModelCalled events still carry per-turn usage. Reconstructible from events but under-reported on the result object; fix while M5 touches Runner for persistence.

No connection pool: every store method opens its own psycopg connection (~15 connect-auth-close cycles per short run), and the calls are synchronous psycopg made from inside the async AgentLoop, so they block the event loop thread. Correct for Phase 0's one-run-at-a-time profile, and the FIRST thing to change before real load -- connect latency would dominate and Postgres max_connections would cap concurrent runs. Fix: psycopg_pool.AsyncConnectionPool plus async store methods; the protocols do not change.

Event sequence_no comes from an in-process counter (len(buffer)+1), so ordering is per SINK INSTANCE, not per run as stored. One process per run makes this correct in Phase 0. It breaks the moment a run resumes in a new process or a second sink observes it: numbering restarts at 1 and collides with UNIQUE (run_id, sequence_no). Phase 6 (durable interruptions, replay) cannot land without moving this into the insert, the way messages.sequence_no already is.

Schema has no migration path: schema.sql is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so it can create a database but cannot evolve one. Any column change in production needs a real migration tool (Alembic or equivalent) before there is data worth keeping.
messages and run_events grow without bound: no retention policy, no partitioning, no archival. Fine at prototype volume; a production deployment needs a plan before the first long-running tenant.

JSONB normalises large floats: a value >= 1e16 written into a JSONB payload reads back as an int, and at 1e308 the returned value compares unequal to the original. Inherent to jsonb's numeric representation, no run fails and no AC is breached, but it is the one demonstrated place where postgres.py's header claim -- that the loop cannot tell whether it is talking to memory or Postgres -- is falsifiable. Found by the M5 round-9 reviewer.

Rejected: SubagentPool._what_it_read calls the new Runner._history_for synchronously, with no asyncio.to_thread or control.store offload, in agentsdk/api.py and agentsdk/subagents.py. On Postgres this is a real psycopg connection checkout plus query, run directly on the event loop while the pool still holds its concurrency slot, right after every child completes. Proved with a probe using a session store whose history() blocks for a fixed delay: two concurrently spawned children finished in about 0.76s instead of about 0.25s, showing the loop was blocked rather than the call being offloaded (probe3_history_blocking.py). controls.human: Sonnet 5 (independent L4 reviewer, M19 round 3, substituted for Fable 5.1 which was out of quota)
controls.reason: Reviewed by Sonnet 5 standing in for Fable 5.1 (out of quota). D6 (medium): the D5 record is built from the version statuses dict, which lags finished tasks. In _execute, when settle raises (a store error on a transition) while a sibling task has already finished but is not yet harvested, the except handler cancels the unharvested running dict and marks that finished node cancelled; the finally in _submit records only statuses done nodes, so a side-effecting node whose child completed and whose output was stored is not in run.done, and the next run_plan that names it runs it again. Reproduced: two side-effecting nodes, first done transition raises once, replan names both, the note tool ran twice for one of them (counts a1 b2, a1 b2, a2 b1 over 3 runs, in memory). Fix: before cancelling in the except branch, harvest tasks that are done, or record done from task results rather than from statuses. Everything else probed held: endings on Postgres (7 scenarios, no run left running, sequences contiguous, no orphans), taint on carried, omitted-then-carried and criterion-text edges, budget sum equals ceiling across 4 versions with carries and skipped nodes, criteria both ways including hang timeout and raise, F2 sinks, demo offline and live read back from Postgres and removed by run id; gate file 47 passed.

D7 blocking: the D6 repair covers only a node task that RETURNED, so the round 3 reproduction still reproduces on the repaired code. Two side-effecting siblings calling a counting tool, the run-state store transition raising once on a version 1 unreasoned done, then a replan naming both: note calls a:1 b:2 (3 calls, not 2), a PlanNodeFinished of b cancelled for a node whose tool had already run, and b run again in version 2. Traced: a returns done, settling it raises, the except branch cancels sibling b while b is inside _attempt after its child had already run the side-effecting tool; task.cancelled() is then true so the harvest loop skips b, the final loop records b cancelled, run.done never gets it and _carried does not carry it. Reproduced repeatedly with no barrier, on the in-memory and the Postgres store; in one variant all three child runs read completed in Postgres while the version 1 node row for b reads cancelled, so the record contradicts itself. The comment at orchestrator.py line 204 states the property of this very path (a node that finished before a raise OR A CANCELLATION has had its side effects all the same) and it is false there. The author test hides the case: pinning the asyncio.wait batch with a barrier over Orchestrator._node makes every task return before the raise, so no in-flight task is present when the except branch runs. This is not in the declared limitations, and side_effecting defaults to True, so it is the harm P2-D18 exists to prevent. Everything else verified sound. I reran both gates myself on source hash 9728e423: unit 48 passed, regression 1587 passed in 281s, and the run_id sets of all seven tables are identical before and after (AC-63). Each half of the D6 repair is independently necessary (no harvest alone gives 3 calls, reverting the settle order alone gives 3, both give 4); every mutation restored by SHA-256. Criteria exercised both ways and each failure names the criterion; critic ends criterion_not_available and reads back from Postgres; a tampered content hash fails ArtifactIntegrityError; an artifact of another run is refused. Taint holds on every edge tried (criterion tool text, carried answer, skipped node, replan) and taking_in only raises taint and lowers trust. Budget sums exactly to the ceiling in USD and in tokens after replans, carries, nodes that never started, a proposer at the cap, six replans and a 1e11 ceiling; for_run plus adopt is identical to the M17 constructor; the D4 clash is refused with state unchanged. FR-76 attribution asserted first hand on both stores: source_run is the child run and source_task is the node id; a model supplied scope is overridden; no schema_hash moves. F2 and F4 verified on Postgres on its own: five misreporting sinks each refused InvalidPlan with nothing changed and no event emitted, a failing emit rolls the row back to pending, three racing transitions recorded Started before Finished every time. Demo 5 of 5 offline and 4 of 4 live, the live run checked in Postgres and removed by its own six run ids. Caveats: a parameter annotated RunScope or None silently receives None, and a RunScope subclass under another name is not injected, because _with_scope matches the annotation by name; a plan_node_states row left running or pending for an abandoned version I judge the right trade-off against a false cancelled, since NFR-22 binds child runs and every child run was terminal in every probe; a criterion check has no deadline and hangs the run.

controls.human: Opus 5 (independent L4 reviewer, M20 round 1, fallback for Fable 5.1 which was out of quota)
controls.reason: Opus 5 reviewed round 1 as the fallback for Fable 5.1, which failed its first API call. Re-derived FR-77, FR-78, AC-61, AC-62, NFR-3, NFR-12, NFR-17 and NFR-21 from SPEC.md and probed all seven attack items first-hand. Gates re-run by me with timeout 590000 on source hash eae1be3a: unit 42 passed in 4.08s, regression 1632 passed in 267.96s, both exit 0, no stray python, and the store back at its baseline of 10351 runs, 6 artifacts, 19 example-tenant runs, 8 migrations, 0 running and 0 orphans. Item 1, 14 of 14: under a policy an agent is sent exactly its profile tools, and a call to any other gives a byte-identical ToolNotFound result and ToolCalled payload to a genuinely unregistered tool, including through a before_model hook that puts every schema back, an empty profile, a profile naming an unregistered tool, and the orchestrator with two children on both stores. Item 2: the same scripted plain run driven against HEAD bf7d0d5 and against M20 produced byte-identical requests, events and history with the same SHA-256, so NFR-12 holds; and equal tools_sent really does imply equal schemas, because schema_hash covers name, description and input schema. Item 3: a fuzzer that never chooses what is replaced ran 90 in-memory and 14 Postgres runs over 334 compactions, varying script, window, kept turns, parallel calls and reported counts, checking the schedule-independent property that compaction k carries the union of the taint and the least trust of everything replaced in compactions 1 to k. Zero failures, and a separate probe showed a child whose only tainted input is its brief still gets an untrusted summary on both stores. The negative is meaningful: the same fuzzer killed 10 of 10 deliberate mutants, among them the first-run survivor the author discloses, which drops the replaced summary taint. Items 4 and 5, both stores: every artifact read back against its hash, replaced indices partitioned with the task never replaced, artifact bodies equal to the stored messages, every stored message surviving, one summary per compaction, usage equal to the sum of ModelCalled and to the lease, sequence_no unique and contiguous, and every request well formed with results after their calls, the task first and at most one summary, through re-asks, parallel calls, a turn larger than the window and up to eleven compactions in one run. Every estimate call of a real run matched the specified formula recomputed by hand on both arms, and the threshold fired on exactly the turns at or above compact_at times the window. Item 6, 14 of 14: model error, three empty-summary shapes, budget refusal with no call sent, provider slot, turn limit, artifact refusal, and cancellation held inside the summarising call 12 of 12 in memory and 3 of 3 on Postgres plus 30 random-timing attempts of which 26 cancelled, all with cost unknown per P2-D7, one RunCancelled last and the stored run cancelled; a mutant dropping the in-flight mark was killed. Item 7: example 18 offline 6 of 6, example 17 offline 5 of 5, example 18 live 6 of 6 read back from Postgres as completed with 17 contiguous events, 2 ContextCompacted, 8 ModelCalled of which 2 summarising, 14 messages holding 2 summaries, tools_sent naming only read_page and both artifacts hash-matched and attributed to the run, then removed by its own run id and artifact ids. The rewritten taint test does pin its premise: it asserts the premise and prints the real sources on failure, its selector is a correct key test, and the mutant it was rewritten for is independently detectable. Non-blocking caveats. C1: tokens_after can be recorded larger than tokens_before, because the two use different bases, a reported count plus a delta against a full estimate; 108 of 330 fuzzed compactions showed it, only where the reported count sits far below characters over four, and the assembled prompt was smaller on all 330 when measured on one basis, so the substance of AC-62 holds while the recorded pair can read backwards, and such under-reporting also makes a run compact on nearly every turn. C2: visibility comes from tool_profile alone, so a spec with a custom permission_policy can be sent a tool its checker denies, or sent nothing while its checker permits tools; this matches the letter of FR-77 and fails closed or to a permission denial, and no shipped example combines the two. C3: the artifact and the summary message are written before the ContextCompacted emit, so a store failure at that point ends the run failed with the reason but leaves a summary in the history with no event; I reproduced it and nothing escaped Runner.run. C4: as declared, tools_sent records what the policy sends and not what a before_model hook substitutes, which I reproduced. C5: the unknown-window refusal reaches a child as node_error at execution time rather than where the run is configured, although the message names the model and the remedy and siblings are unaffected. C6: the M19 caveats carry forward unprobed, since M20 does not touch that code. Approved.

Re-derived FR-85, FR-86, AC-68, AC-69 from SPEC.md and read the diff against a576adc. Recomputed both gates: genesis gate --timeout 590000 gave unit 15 passed and regression 1647 passed on live source hash f19dc611, which I recomputed with the Genesis file walk after the run; the full suite also passed on its own, 1647 in 324s. All six attack items probed first-hand with scripts under SYN-m20ar1 tenants, every run removed by id, store back at baseline (10351 runs, 6 artifacts, 0 SYN, 19 example-tenant, 0 running). Item 1: on Postgres I failed the messages lock, the message insert before and after its row, the events lock, the event insert after its row, the COMMIT itself (backend terminated from another connection) and stored() after the commit; every case left no summary without its event and no event without its summary, run status failed with the store error, both sequences contiguous, the artifact untrusted and named by nothing; a runtime two-transaction mutant was detected. In memory, append and emit failures left neither. Item 2: 10 rounds of nine concurrent appenders, emitters and combined writers plus a run-row updater on one run, 900 messages and 900 events, 0 errors, contiguous; a deliberate opposite-order writer produced DeadlockDetected 5 of 5, so the probe can see a deadlock; append_with_event is the only SDK transaction taking two run locks, so no cycle exists. Item 3: 12 runs with parallel tool calls and 96 compactions, the handle stream equal to RunResult.events equal to the stored rows on both stores. Item 4: 530 compactions over 92 random schedules on both stores, the pair recomputed from the requests the model received plus the artifacts and the decider from the previous report, 0 mismatches; three mutants (a lying basis, an estimator off by one, the M20 shape) all caught. Item 5: custom store fallback on both stores with the declared gap shown; foreign-run and foreign-tenant sinks refused on Postgres; PublishingSink offers write and stored only over a sink that has both. Item 6: demo offline 6 of 6 and live 6 of 6, the live run read back from Postgres (two summaries, two events, contiguous, printed pair and decider equal to the stored payload) and removed by id. Readings (a) to (f) judged sound. Caveats, low, not blockers, for the next task: (C7) InMemorySessionStore.append_with_event does None[2] when the sink is a PublishingSink over a custom sink without scope, failing the run with a TypeError where Postgres falls back and M20 completed; reachable only through a custom persistence pairing an in-memory session store with a scopeless sink. (C8) the in-memory check compares only the run id, so a sink for another tenant with the same run id is accepted; Postgres and refuse_foreign_sink compare the whole triple; reachable only by direct misuse. (C9) a failed combined write also leaves the ModelCalled event with purpose compaction, a true record of a charged call, so the artifact is not literally the only leftover. (C10) a stored() failure after the commit leaves both rows and an in-process RunResult lacking the event; not reachable in practice. Enlarging compactions: 11 of 530, all when a constant large provider count decided on a tiny replaceable middle; surfacing it is sufficient, and a compaction that would replace nothing is skipped so no loop is possible.

One reachable regression in the in-memory binding seam. InMemorySessionStore._unbound iterates self._runs in a list comprehension (session.py) on every unbound append, history and append_with_event. Worker threads insert keys concurrently (setdefault in bound appends), so the iteration raises RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration. Before M21 these calls were a single dict lookup and could not raise. Reproduced: a real Runner holding about 1300 finished runs, an unbound runner._sessions.history(run_id) polled while 300 other runs wrote: 4 of 15 attempts raised; 3000 runs: 6 of 15; 20000 runs: 7 of 10; 300 runs: 0 of 10. Unbound appends, the retained path for an application driving the loop itself: 8 threads, 2400 runs in the store, 7 of 10 attempts raised appends (0 of 13 on the pre-M21 session.py at the same sizes); each unbound call is also an O(runs) scan (12000 runs, 36000 appends, 8 to 17 s). Fix: keep a run_id to keys index under a lock, or snapshot with list(self._runs) which is atomic, and add a concurrent test. Everything else probed held: F1/F2 matrix on both stores (14 sink shapes, nothing written before any refusal, take-back kept, mutant that disables the check detected), 25 of 25 concurrent 16-run iterations keep per-tenant histories separate (unbound-key mutant detected), 15 of 15 nested orchestrator runs correct, C6 (no side effect in _open, nothing stored before refusal on Postgres, replan refused, unused bad role not refused, mutant detected), C4 and C5 declarations faithful. Caveats: the binding is visible inside the PublishingSink publish callback on the loop (copied context), benign today; gate on source hash 01e7b5ba re-run green, 1664 passed.

Round 2 verified first-hand on source hash 1c386e0f: unit 18 passed and regression 1665 passed from my own genesis gate run with --timeout 590000, the full suite also run directly with no cacheprovider (1665 passed), the live contentHash recomputed and equal to the evidence, no stray python. Round 1 defect: the round-1 shape (6 binders, 6 unbound appenders and readers, 1us switch interval) 0 of 10 attempts on the repair, and a mixed shape with bound and unbound appends, reads and take-backs racing on the same run ids 0 of 10; detectors: the scan restored outside the lock reproduced 8 of 8 at 1us and only 1 of 8 at the default 5ms (the author disclosure holds), 4 of 4 in the mixed shape; the index not kept detected 4 of 4; emit moved under the lock deadlocked the re-entrant probe within 10s; every mutant restored byte for byte and SHA-256 verified, no debris. Lock: one non-reentrant lock, never nested, never held across emit; a sink whose emit calls the store on the same thread, or on another thread and waits for it, completes; the take-back runs under the lock and releases it; the by_run index is written only in the one locked insert and nothing deletes, so it cannot drift from the dict, checked after every attempt. F1 and F2: 11 sink shapes bound and unbound in memory and 14 on Postgres; scope-less and PublishingSink shapes get both writes with the take-back kept; a foreign run, tenant or project is refused before anything is written; Postgres sequence numbers contiguous after. C6: Runner._open with persistence makes no row, no connection checkout and no started record; an unknown window, reasoning without max_output_tokens and an unpriced model under a USD ceiling are each refused at submission naming the role; a runnable role is not refused; a replan naming a role the first plan did not name is refused on both stores, version 2 never stored and no child spawned for it; carried nodes skipped correctly. C4 and C5 declarations faithful, the C5 qualifier checked without a policy. Regressions: 6 concurrent in-memory runs compacting under 4 unbound reader threads and a binder, 3 of 3 attempts clean with each history filed under its own tenant only; a handle consumer and a tool reading the store unbound while runs proceed, the binding None outside store calls; orchestrations with a replan completed on both stores with a whole Postgres record; the 5 example scripts holding unbound history reads ran offline with exit 0 and the 42 test call sites ran in the suite. Caveats, latent, not blockers: on the unbound path append_with_event derives the key twice, so an unbound combined write racing the first bound write of the same new run id can leave the message behind on a failed emit and double-index the id; an unbound append to a Runner run id before the Runner first writes splits the id so later unbound reads are refused (171 of 200 in a race) where HEAD merged them; both need a caller writing into a Runner-bound run from outside, which no product path or call site does. The binding stays set during sink.emit inside a bound combined write, so a sink that itself writes another run to the same store on that thread is refused; no shipped sink touches the session store. All rows removed by recorded run ids; the store is at its baseline.

Re-derived FR-97 and AC-75 from SPEC.md and ran both gates myself: unit 10 passed, regression 1675 passed in 279.87s, exit 0, source hash 8ade0977 matching the live tree. Caveats 1 and 2 probed first-hand rather than accepted: 2800 contended attempts at a 1 microsecond switch interval over six races (two tenants binding one id, a bound read racing an unbound write, an adoption racing a take-back, unbound combined writes with recorded and with failing sinks racing the first bound write, and a combined write while two tenants bind) found no run id filed under two keys, no summary left without its event, and no disagreement between the two indexes, checked after every attempt. All fourteen deterministic interleavings, with a second tenant writing at each of the four seams of the combined write, also held. Nine mutants, each restored byte for byte with its SHA-256 verified in a finally: the gate file killed all nine, my probe killed four of the seven aimed at the store, and the same probe at the default 5 millisecond interval found nothing where it found 54 violations at a microsecond, so the negatives are measured. The two indexes cannot disagree because every mutation of both happens in one critical section and adoption replaces the unbound entry in place. Adoption on a read is sound: it creates nothing for an unwritten run, still returns a copy, and only decides which tenant adopts, which is the declared rule. The lock is a plain lock, never nested and never held across emit; a sink whose emit calls the store on the same thread, or waits on another thread that does, completes. Caveat 3 is faithful: instrumenting AgentLoop at the class saw exactly the four loops the test sees, there is one construction site, and a mutant that builds a foreign sink is detected. Caveat 4 is faithful and its test detects an inverted write order. The manual edit of project.json is exactly what DECISION-23ae5809 discloses and nothing more, re-derived with a structural diff. Three caveats, none blocking: the README row for caveat 4 names only a scope-less sink while a custom sink that names the run but has no write and stored takes the same two-write path; an unbound combined write compares only the run id against a scoped sink, so with adoption its summary can land in the history of whichever tenant binds the id first while the event goes to the sink it named, reachable only by code driving the loop with an unbound store; and a bound read now moves a key, a read with a side effect. Database and tree restored to the baseline.

Probes in scratchpad m22-r1-probes with tenants SYN-m22r1, every row removed by run id: the reach rule compared SQL vs in-memory vs reaches() vs a spec oracle over 112 versions x 48 reader and key combinations with zero mismatch, get() filtered by tenant and project on both stores; SESSION across tenants or projects sharing a ledger id and across top-level runs misses on both stores while a run carrying the top-level ledger is served; a PUBLIC_GLOBAL copy carries only hash, retrieval time, final_uri and media type, origin rows untouched, no foreign id in any column or event; a consistently forged artifact (content and artifact hash both rewritten) is still a miss against the version hash on both stores; no UPDATE or DELETE names source_versions; a store failure after the artifact put leaves no version and an error the model sees; no URL that _target admits makes canonical_uri raise; host_scopes applies by normalised host; future-dated and clock-skewed versions are never served and become the prior; default boundary served at 3599s and refetched at 3600s on Postgres; outside a Runner 29 outcomes and 3 tool specs are byte-identical to HEAD fa64753 and the default schema_hash 1c16f3bc is unchanged; ledger_run_id is the top-level id for a top-level run, a child and a grandchild spawned from really injected ToolScopes, and for orchestrator children before and after a replan; 40 memory and 10 Postgres trials of 8 parallel fetches of one key plus 6 concurrent runs of two tenants at a 1 microsecond switch interval with REFUSE_ON_EVENT_LOOP on: nothing raised, no on-loop store call, accounting consistent, no cross-tenant read; the C2 repair read and its test fails without it; example 19 live 6 of 6 against example.com and the gateway, rows removed by run id. Requirements re-derived from SPEC.md FR-92 to FR-94, NFR-25, NFR-26, AC-73. Verified first-hand: full suite 1864 passed (435 s, no cacheprovider); genesis gate with timeout 590000 passed, evidence source_hash fb7c130d unchanged, no stray python; example 20 offline 7 of 7; migration 0011 checksum matches file, tables at 0 rows at baseline; project.json diff 8ba3b01 shows only 2 decisions added, 2 requeue controls, no task added removed or reordered. claim_key is one Python function used by both stores, identical across 3 processes and hash seeds over every code point; AC-73 pairs (case, spacing, NFC/NFD, ss) give one key. Concurrency at switchinterval 1e-6, 30 attempts per phase on both stores (record x8, 6-way supersede, record racing supersede) plus 3 OS processes on one DB (20 attempts): 0 duplicate claims, 0 forks, 0 contributions after supersession (xmin order); no-lock mutants fail in every column, so the probes detect. Taint: history, briefed input, orchestrator child answer and uri-cited versions all reach the claim as untrusted; no-taken-in mutant flips it. Tenancy: cross-tenant and cross-project uri and URL citations refused, other tenant project ledger reads empty, cross-ledger supersede refused; foreign-version mutant flips. Cite-by-URL right after redirect, cache hit by a child, tenant copy, stale refetch, spellings (default port, trailing dot, fragment); other-run URL refused. M22 caveats 1 to 5 sound; caveat 4 shown with a no-delete mutant (artifact left 0 vs 1); canonical_uri differs from M22 only in host. CAVEATS not blockers: (1) the store layer does not enforce what RunLedger does: LedgerStore.record on both stores accepts a contribution citing another tenants version, a run id from another tenant, and a provenance lower than the cited versions (NFR-25 and NFR-26 hold only through RunLedger); the 0011 comment saying the store checks the cited versions tenant is untrue, and there are no DB triggers so append-only rests on the API surface; fix in code, do not edit the migration (checksum). (2) Two supersessions whose sorted key pairs cross-collide in hashtext (found with 450k keys, 20 collisions) raised DeadlockDetected instead of waiting, no corruption, needs crafted statements. (3) A briefed input carrying an older version urn outranks the runs own newer fetch when citing by URL, contrary to newest tool result in history; only reachable by briefing a cache artifact. (4) Case-only variants of 8 Greek characters give different keys because NFC then casefold is not canonically closed; follows the spec literally; zero-width and full-width forms are distinct keys. (5) every record reads the whole ledger back, quadratic in ledger size.

Requirements re-derived from SPEC.md FR-95, FR-96, NFR-24, NFR-25, AC-74 and the M24 sentences of FR-92 and FR-93. Gates recomputed by me on source hash 0c9970bd: unit 27 passed, regression 1891 passed in 404 s, both exit 0, no stray python; a separate full suite gave 1891 passed in 370 s. All eight attack items probed first-hand. Singleflight: 40 trials of 8 tasks at a 1 microsecond switch interval never had two holders; 5 OS processes on one database fetched one page once with 4 waiters served and took_result true, and a second tenant added exactly one more fetch, while a no-lock mutant gave 5 and 8 fetches, so the probe detects the defect. Retry: 25 trials gave exactly 1 plus 3 operations, 3 delays inside 0.2, 0.4 and 0.8 s, 5 waiters failing by key name and a fresh call clean; a cancelled holder is retried and the waiters succeed; a waiter failing after a good holder does not poison the key. Cancellation: 128 sweep attempts, 60 cancelled-waiter trials and 24 public-API trials with the cancel timed into the window between pg_try_advisory_lock succeeding and its result arriving, all leaving 0 advisory locks and the pool idle; pg_locks and other connections were 0 before and after every probe and 0 at the end. A waiting call holds no connection and adds no measurable loop delay; a tool timeout counted the wait and reported ToolTimeout at 5985 ms while the holder still fetched once. Cross-process: taskkill of a holder freed the key in 0.28 s, and hashtext collisions only cost waiting. Tenancy: both lock keys name tenant and project, SESSION carries the ledger run, NO_CACHE takes no lock. Exit signal: example 21 on 7 seeds of my own on both stores, 7 of 7 checks each, 177 to 208 claim-lock waits, so it contends in fact. M23 caveats: both stores now refuse cross-tenant, cross-project and unknown citations and raise a deliberately trusted clean contribution to untrusted with both taint flags; normalised is idempotent over every Unicode code point; the hash-ordered lock serialised 30 of 30 crossing-collision trials where the restored text-sorted lock deadlocked 30 of 30. Governance: the diff adds only DECISION-eecef939, knowledge stays at 107, 28 tasks unchanged in order, state and content, controls 85 to 86 with one requeue, no migration edited and all 10 checksums match their files. Caveats, none reachable through the public surface. First, ClaimLock _completed suppresses a re-delivered CancelledError, so a cancellation delivered twice while it is undoing drops the holder connection without pg_advisory_unlock or putconn, leaving an advisory lock held until the garbage collector closes the socket and losing one pool slot for good; 33 such events exhausted the pool and the next store call raised PoolTimeout after 30 s. RunControl request is guarded and RunHandle result shields the run task, so the public API delivers only one cancellation and this needs code outside NFR-5. Second, lock keys are joined with a vertical bar and tenant ids are unvalidated, so tenant A-bar-p with project x and tenant A with project p-bar-x share one key, letting a wait, though never a result, cross a tenant; the pattern predates M24. Third, _retry catches Exception only, so a cancelled retrier leaves no attempt budget. Fourth, a waiter failing after a good holder opens a fresh 3-attempt budget. Fifth, a call that waited and got a non-2xx response records no event, so its wait is unrecorded. Sixth, the holder keeps a pooled connection while its operation draws on the same pool of 32. Seventh, the task requirement list omits NFR-25. The six open choices are all sound: serialised waiters, per-process retry state, k counting from 0, supersede without a claim-lock since the hash-ordered store lock serialises it, the took_result mapping, and the editor citing nothing, the last weakening the exit signal slightly because the corrected claim cites no source and its taint check therefore passes vacuously.

Re-derived FR-98 and AC-76. Gates recomputed by the reviewer: unit 9 passed, regression 1900 passed in 347.72s, both on source hash 880b57dd, no stray process. C1: 48 trials on the live database cancelling 1, 2, 5 and 20 times at every await (asyncio lock wait, try-lock before and after taking the lock, contended try-lock, poll sleep, holding, normal release, release after a failed op, undo, retry backoff, retry op) left no advisory lock in pg_locks, every pooled connection returned, every call returning only after its release thread finished, CancelledError raised each time; the same probe with M24 _completed swapped in reports a held lock, a stuck checkout and early returns. wait_for and asyncio.timeout raise TimeoutError only after the release; an extra cancel gives CancelledError. C3 and C4: a 400-seed fuzz of ok, fail, cancel-in-op and cancel-in-backoff on one key never exceeds three attempts and every later call fails naming the key, while the M24 module breaks 95 seeds, worst 11. C2: 20000 random part lists give no lock_key collision where a pipe join gives 168; both call sites pass strings; two reaches whose names pipe-join alike get different keys. M22, M23 and M24 gate files pass (215). The gate file fails 4 tests with M24 _completed and 2 with M24 _retry swapped in through a plugin. Caveats, none blocking: a retrier cancelled during its backoff delay draws an attempt, so three such cancellations fail the key with no operation retried; the budget is not restored by a success while calls remain on the key, so under uninterrupted contention one later failure fails the key with no retry once three are spent; a try-lock or release thread that never returns keeps the call uncancellable and delays a tool timeout for as long as it takes (2 s shown; pool checkout is bounded at 30 s, a query on a dead link is not), the same property as every store call; in Python 3.11 a wait_for whose timeout already fired and is then cancelled returns before the inner release ends, which still completes; KeyFailed shows no cause when the key was failed through failed_once or a cancelled retry; the M23 transaction-lock pipe join is an acceptable leftover since a collision only serialises two writers on one lock value (shown) and the claim-lock keys differ, best fixed when that test is next edited.

Verified first hand, not from the recorded evidence. My own genesis gate run on source hash 10b16da7 gives unit 14 passed in 2.68s and regression 1914 passed in 321.33s, exit 0, no stray python; 1914 collected equals the 1900 baseline plus the 14 new tests, and the M22, M23, M24 and M24a gate files together with M25 give 238 passed. B1 with FR-98: the bound is absolute, 3 operations after the first failure with 26 waiters cancelled in their backoff while every call stayed on the key, and a mutant that restores the budget on a cancelled backoff breaks it to 5, so the probe is not vacuous; removing the line that charges a failed backoff hangs forever, so that guard is needed. K1: the cause is the failure that spent the last attempt on all four paths and never an earlier KeyFailed, and a mutant raising from the stored KeyFailed is caught. P1, P2 and NFR-29: no delimiter join feeds a hash or a lock name anywhere, agent_spec_hash is TEXT with no length or hex constraint and no reader assumes 64 hex, the two 64 hex checks are on content_hash and claim_key only, and an ungated run on PostgreSQL records the same status, the same events and the same rows as the committed pre-M25 tree with agent_spec_hash the only difference; both P2 assertions bite under mutation and the old pipe join really did collide. C5: on both stores a waited fetch answered 404 and 500 emits exactly one SourceUncached, an unwaited one and a 2xx emit none, the payload is canonical uri, status and the wait, stored as jsonb and read back, and no wait crosses a tenant or a project; dropping the wait guard is caught. Example 21: seven checks pass on both stores, taint_holds is false for a clean claim citing a tainted page, for an untrusted claim missing its flags and for no claims, the combined check fails on both stores when the correction cites nothing, so it is not vacuous, and a cited version uri is refused from another tenant and from another project. The edit to the approved caveat-2 test is necessary, the old form fails against the new code, and it is not weakening: reverting the lock names to the pipe join, reversing the order and dropping DISTINCT each make it fail by assertion. The one manual edit to project.json is structurally just a regression gate on the four increment 2 tasks, same key order, command and position as the gates the CLI wrote, with every other delta CLI shaped. CAVEAT 1, the one finding: _finished treats future.done() as proof that an exception is the futures own outcome, which is false for the two loop hops between the worker task finishing and the interrupted task resuming; a cancellation or a hand delivered KeyboardInterrupt arriving there is dropped and _completed returns the workers value, so an asyncio timeout around a claim-lock call silently does not fire. Reproduced 3 of 3 with a real worker thread on PostgreSQL and 3 of 3 with timeout_at on a bare future; the committed pre-M25 code does not drop it, so this is a regression inside the W2 repair, and it is also why the dropped mutant cannot be killed, 41 tests pass with it applied. No lock or connection leaked in any case, 0 advisory locks and 0 pooled connections after 1, 2, 5 and 25 cancellations, so FR-98 C1 holds, and 0 of 400 naturally timed trials hit the window, which is why I treat it as a caveat rather than a blocker: it is strictly milder than the declared W1. The repair is to stop continuing on a CancelledError when the future is not cancelled, and the FR-99 sentence that the threads future is done only in the second case is false and needs correcting. CAVEAT 2: the authors judgement that the dropped mutant is equivalent is right for the case argued, the works own exception raises identically either way, but it is not semantically equivalent and the mutant is the better code. CAVEAT 3, cosmetic: KeyFailed sets __cause__ in __init__, which also sets __suppress_context__ true even when the cause is None, so a KeyFailed raised inside an except block hides its context, and unpickling one puts the whole message in key; both pre-existing in shape. All eight files I mutated restored and SHA-256 verified identical, git status unchanged, 71 probe runs and their rows removed by run id only, store back at baseline, no advisory lock held, no stray process.

Round 3 reject. NFR-39 hole in agentsdk/mcp/__init__.py: aclose marks the loop closed and pops connections, but _Connection.close() never sets dead, and the Tool closures built earlier still hold the old _Connection. A tool call that begins after aclose (the model answers after the Runner closed, or a second call in the same turn follows a slow one) enters _call, sees client None, runs ensure(), starts<2 and dead False, so it starts a NEW server. That server is in no connection map: a second aclose does not stop it. Reproduced on a Runner: aclose while the model was thinking, run completed, new server pid alive after aclose and after a second aclose; same with McpClients directly. The round 3 test only covers the next-turn refresh path, not a tool object already handed out. Fix: close() must set dead, and ensure() must refuse when its loop is in _closed. Second defect, same file, discard path: after a wedge discard, a call from another run arriving during the old task teardown (about 2 s) restarts the server, then the old serve task finally sets self.client to None on the NEW connection. Reproduced: later call fails mcp server exited with the second server alive and unused, and the restart budget spent. Fix: guard the finally by task identity and let _call keep its own client reference. Caveats not alone rejecting: a loop stall of 1.6 s or more across call_timeout lets the SDK deadline win over a healthy honest timeout and discards the connection (measured, 0.7 s stall kept it); a crash then restart leaves the first serve task running after aclose; the conftest fixture imports private _pytest.faulthandler for all tests unguarded.
